name: Ezekiel
sourceNote: Translated fresh from the Hebrew of the Westminster Leningrad Codex, with the Greek Septuagint (Brenton's public-domain edition) compared throughout. The Septuagint of Ezekiel is noticeably shorter than the Hebrew (it lacks, for example, 1:14, 10:14, and 40:30), and footnotes flag significant differences. Papyrus 967, a very early Greek manuscript of Ezekiel, is reported in scholarly literature to lack 36:23c–38 and to place chapter 37 after chapters 38–39; these reports are cited as reported and have not been checked against the papyrus itself. Ezekiel dates many of his oracles; each date is given in the text with its modern month span (from the spring new year), with the original month in a footnote. In the temple vision (chapters 40–48) measurements use Ezekiel's "long cubit" (a standard cubit plus a handbreadth, about 21 inches or 53 cm) and his measuring reed of six long cubits (about 10.5 feet or 3.2 m); figures in the text are converted to US units, with the original units and metric figures in footnotes. "Son of man" (Hebrew ben adam) is kept as Yahweh's address to the prophet because of its New Testament echoes; it means "human one, mortal." Verse numbers follow the standard English versification. This is a draft awaiting scholarly review.

verses.text: In the thirtieth year,{a} on the fifth day of the fourth month (in June–July),{b} while I was among the exiles beside the Chebar canal,{c} the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth of the month—it was the fifth year since King Jehoiachin had been taken into exile{d}—
the word of Yahweh came expressly to Ezekiel{e} the priest, son of Buzi,{f} in the land of the Chaldeans by the Chebar canal, and there the hand of Yahweh came upon him.

As I watched, a storm wind was sweeping in from the north: an immense cloud with fire flashing back and forth, a radiance surrounding it, and at its center something that gleamed like glowing metal{g} in the heart of the fire.
Within it was the form of four living creatures, and this was how they looked: they had a human shape,
but each one had four faces, and each had four wings.
Their legs were straight, and their feet were shaped like a calf's hoof; they glittered like burnished bronze.
Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands. As for the faces and wings of all four,
their wings touched one another. They did not turn as they moved; each went straight ahead.
The form of their faces was this: each of the four had a human face in front, a lion's face on the right, an ox's face on the left, and an eagle's face as well.
Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above; each creature had two wings touching those of its neighbor and two covering its body.
Each moved directly forward. Where the spirit{h} was to go, there they went; they never turned in their going.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like torches. Fire moved to and fro among the creatures; the fire was bright, and lightning shot out of it.
And the living creatures darted back and forth like flashes of lightning.{i}
While I gazed at the living creatures, I noticed one wheel on the ground next to each creature, by all four of them.
The wheels and their construction looked like the sparkle of chrysolite;{j} all four had the same form, and they were built as though one wheel were set inside another.
In moving they went toward any one of their four sides and did not swing around while going.
Their rims were tall and fearsome, and the rims of all four were covered with eyes all around.
When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them; when the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose too.
Where the spirit was to go, there they went, and the wheels lifted up together with them, because the spirit of the living creature{k} was in the wheels.

When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they stood still, the wheels stood still; when they rose from the ground, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
Over the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of a vault,{l} gleaming like awe-inspiring crystal, stretched out above their heads.
Beneath the vault their wings were stretched straight out, one toward another; each creature also had two wings covering its body on one side and two on the other.
When they moved, I heard the sound of their wings like the roar of vast waters, like the voice of Shaddai,{m} a tumult like the noise of an army. When they stood still, they let their wings drop.
Then a voice came from above the vault over their heads; whenever they stood still, they lowered their wings.
Above the vault that was over their heads there was the likeness of a throne, like lapis lazuli in appearance,{n} and seated above on that likeness of a throne was a likeness with a human appearance.

From what looked like his waist upward I saw something like gleaming metal, with what seemed to be fire enclosing it all around; and from what looked like his waist downward I saw what seemed to be fire, with brightness surrounding him.

As the bow that appears in a cloud on a day of rain looks, so looked the brightness that surrounded him. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of Yahweh. When I saw it, I fell facedown, and I heard the voice of someone speaking.

notes.text: The reference point of "the thirtieth year" is uncertain. It may be Ezekiel's age (the age at which priests began service, Num 4:3), or it may be counted from some other event, such as Josiah's reform.

Hebrew: "in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month." Months are counted from the spring new year; the fourth month (later called Tammuz) fell in June–July. On the date given in v. 2 this was 593 BC.
Or "river." The Chebar was a canal of the Euphrates near Nippur in Babylonia.
That is, 593 BC. Jehoiachin was deported to Babylon in 597 BC (2 Kgs 24:10–15); Ezekiel counts his dates from this exile.
Ezekiel means "God strengthens" or "may God strengthen." The Greek has "Jezekiel."
Buzi may mean "my contempt"; the meaning is uncertain.
Hebrew hashmal, a rare word of uncertain meaning; the Greek has "amber" (electrum). Also in v. 27.
Or "wind"; also in v. 20.
Verse 14 is not found in the Greek (Septuagint).
Hebrew tarshish, a precious stone of uncertain identity, perhaps beryl or topaz.
Or "the spirit of life"; "living creature" here is singular, perhaps referring to the creatures as a whole.
Or "platform," "expanse"; the same word as in Gen 1:6.
Shaddai is a divine name, traditionally "the Almighty"; its original meaning is uncertain. The Greek lacks "like the voice of Shaddai."
Hebrew sappir, probably lapis lazuli rather than the modern sapphire.

verses.text: He said to me, "Son of man,{a} stand up on your feet, and I will speak with you."
While he was speaking with me, the Spirit came into me and stood me upright, and I listened to the one who addressed me.
He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the people of Israel, to rebellious nations that have rebelled against me. They and their ancestors have revolted against me to this very day.
The descendants are hard-faced and stubborn-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says.'
Whether they hear or hold back—since they are a house of rebels—they will come to know that a prophet has lived among them.

As for you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or of their words. Even though briars and thorns surround you and you sit among scorpions, do not fear their words or be shaken by their looks, for they are a rebellious house.
You are to speak my words to them whether they listen or refuse, for they are rebellious.
"But you, son of man, listen to what I am telling you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."
Then I looked, and a hand was stretched out to me, and in it was a written scroll.
He spread it open in front of me; it was inscribed inside and out, and on it were written laments, mourning, and woe.

notes.text: Hebrew ben adam, "son of a human being," an idiom meaning "human one" or "mortal." It stresses the prophet's frailty before God and is used about ninety times in Ezekiel. The traditional rendering is kept because of the related expression in Dan 7:13 and Jesus' use of "the Son of Man" in the Gospels.

verses.text: He said to me, "Son of man, eat what is in front of you. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel."
So I opened my mouth, and he fed me the scroll.
He said to me, "Son of man, let your stomach take in this scroll I give you, and fill your insides with it." So I ate, and in my mouth it tasted sweet as honey.
Then he said to me, "Son of man, go now to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.
It is not to a nation of strange lips and heavy tongue that you are sent, but to the house of Israel—
not to many peoples of unintelligible speech and hard language whose words you could not understand. Surely, if I had sent you to them, they would listen to you.
But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, because they are not willing to listen to me; the whole house of Israel has a hard forehead and a stubborn heart.
Look, I am making your face firm to match their faces, and your brow firm to match their brows.
I have made your forehead like a diamond,{a} harder than flint. Do not fear them or be dismayed by their looks, for they are a rebellious house."
He said to me, "Son of man, take to heart all my words that I speak to you, and listen closely.
Go now to the exiles, to your own people. Speak to them and tell them, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says,' whether they listen or refuse."
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and behind me I heard a great roaring sound: "Blessed be the glory of Yahweh from his place!"{b}
What I heard was the wings of the living creatures beating against each other and the rumbling of the wheels next to them, a great roaring noise.
The Spirit lifted me and took me away, and I went in bitterness, in the heat of my spirit, with the hand of Yahweh pressing hard on me.
I came to the exiles at Tel-abib,{c} the ones living beside the Chebar canal. I sat where they were sitting, and I remained there among them seven days, overwhelmed.
At the end of seven days the word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, I have set you as a lookout for Israel's house. Whenever a word comes from my mouth, you are to warn them for me.

If I tell a wicked man, 'You will surely die,' and you give him no warning—if you say nothing to warn him away from his wicked course so as to save his life—that wicked man will die in his guilt, but I will require his blood from your hand.
But if you do warn the wicked, and he does not turn back from his wickedness and his evil course, he will die in his guilt, but you will have rescued your own life.

Again, when a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, and I put a stumbling block before him, he will die. Because you did not warn him, he will die for his sin; the righteous deeds he did will not be remembered, but I will hold you responsible for his blood.
But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live because he took the warning, and you will have saved your life."
There the hand of Yahweh came upon me, and he said to me, "Get up and go out to the valley,{d} and there I will speak with you."
So I got up and went out to the valley, and there stood the glory of Yahweh, like the glory I had seen by the Chebar canal; and I fell facedown.
Then the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.
As for you, son of man, ropes will be put on you, and you will be bound with them so that you cannot go out among them.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth so that you will be mute and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious house.

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says.' Whoever will listen, let him listen; whoever will refuse, let him refuse; for they are a rebellious house."

notes.text: Hebrew shamir, a very hard stone, perhaps emery or diamond.
With a slight change of one letter, the Hebrew could read "as the glory of Yahweh rose from its place," which many scholars prefer.
In Hebrew Tel-abib suggests "mound of ripe grain"; it is probably a Hebrew form of a Babylonian name meaning "mound of the flood," that is, an ancient ruin mound.
Or "plain."

verses.text: "Now you, son of man, take a clay brick, set it before you, and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem.
Lay siege to it: build siege works against it, heap up a ramp against it, set up camps against it, and position battering rams against it all around.

Next take an iron baking plate and stand it up as a wall of iron separating you from the city. Set your face against it, so that it is under siege and you are its besieger. This will be a sign to the house of Israel.
"Next, lie down on your left side and place on it the guilt of the house of Israel. As many days as you lie on that side, you will carry their guilt.
I have assigned you a number of days matching the years of their guilt: three hundred ninety days.{a} So you will bear the guilt of the house of Israel.
When you have completed these, lie down a second time, on your right side, and bear the guilt of the house of Judah forty days—a day for each year; I have assigned it to you.
Fix your gaze on besieged Jerusalem, bare your arm, and prophesy against the city.
Look, I am tying you with cords, and you will not roll from one side to the other until you finish the days of your siege.

"Now take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt; put them together in a single jar and bake your bread from them. All the days you are lying on your side—three hundred ninety days—you will eat it.
The food you eat will be weighed out: about eight ounces{b} a day. You will eat it at set times.
You will also drink water by measure, about two-thirds of a quart{c} a day; drink it at set times.
Eat it as you would a barley cake, baking it in their sight over human dung."
And Yahweh said, "This is how the people of Israel will eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them."
Then I said, "Ah, Lord Yahweh! I have never been made unclean. Since boyhood I have not eaten the flesh of an animal that died naturally or was mauled, and no foul meat has passed my lips."
So he said to me, "Very well, I will let you use cow dung instead of human dung; prepare your bread over that."
He also said to me, "Son of man, I am about to break the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and with anxiety, and drink water by measure and in dismay,
so that they will lack bread and water, stare at one another in horror, and waste away in their guilt.

notes.text: The Greek has "one hundred ninety days" here and in v. 9, and "one hundred fifty days" in v. 4.
Hebrew: "twenty shekels" (about 230 grams).
Hebrew: "a sixth of a hin" (about 0.6 liter).

verses.text: "As for you, son of man, take a sharp sword and use it as a barber's razor; pass it over your head and your beard. Then take scales for weighing and divide the hair.

A third you are to burn with fire in the middle of the city when the siege days are over. A third you are to take and cut up with the sword around the city. A third you are to scatter to the wind, and I will draw a sword to pursue them.
Take from them a few strands and tuck them into the folds of your garment.
Then take some more of them, cast them into the fire, and let them burn. Out of that fire a blaze will go forth against the whole house of Israel.
"This is what the Lord Yahweh says: This is Jerusalem. I placed her at the center of the nations, with countries all around her.

But she has rebelled against my judgments more wickedly than the nations, and against my statutes more than the countries around her; for they have rejected my judgments and have not walked in my statutes.

"Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you have been more turbulent than the nations around you, have not walked in my statutes or carried out my judgments, and have not even acted by the standards of the nations around you,{a}
therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I, I myself, am against you. I will carry out judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.
For all your abominations I will deal with you in a way I have not dealt before and in a way I will never deal again.
So parents will eat their children in your midst, and children will eat their parents. I will execute judgments on you and scatter all your survivors to every wind.

Therefore, as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and all your abominations, I myself will withdraw;{b} my eye will not spare, and I will have no pity.

A third of your people will die by plague or perish of hunger inside your walls; a third will be cut down by the sword outside them; and the last third I will scatter in all directions, drawing a sword to pursue them.
"Then my anger will be spent, and I will satisfy my fury on them and be appeased. And they will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken in my zeal, when I have spent my fury on them.
I will turn you into a wasteland and an object of scorn among the surrounding nations, before the eyes of everyone who travels past.

You will become a disgrace and a thing of mockery, an object lesson and a horror to the nations about you, when I bring judgments upon you with anger, fury, and furious punishments. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
When I shoot at them the deadly arrows of famine, arrows meant to destroy, which I will send to destroy you, I will increase the famine on you and break your supply of bread.

I will send against you famine and savage beasts that will rob you of your children. Pestilence and blood will pass through your streets, and I will bring a sword down on you. I, Yahweh, have spoken."

notes.text: Some ancient witnesses lack "not," reading "but have acted by the standards of the nations" (compare 11:12).
Or "I will cut you down"; the Hebrew verb is uncertain.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

Say, 'Mountains of Israel, listen to the word of the Lord Yahweh. The Lord Yahweh speaks this way to mountains and hills, to gorges and valleys: Look, I myself will bring a sword upon you and wipe out your high places.{a}
Your altars will be laid waste and your incense stands broken; and the slain among you I will throw down before your idols.{b}
I will lay the corpses of the people of Israel before their idols and scatter your bones around your altars.

Wherever you live, the towns will be laid waste and the high places made desolate, so that your altars will be wrecked and ruined, your idols smashed and gone, your incense stands cut down, and your handiwork wiped out.
The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am Yahweh.
"'Yet I will leave a remnant: some of you will escape the sword among the nations when you are scattered through the countries.

Then those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they are held captive—how I was crushed by their unfaithful hearts that turned away from me, and by their eyes that went lusting after their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evils they have done, for all their abominations.
And they will know that I am Yahweh; I did not threaten in vain to bring this disaster on them.'

"This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Clap your hands and stamp your feet and cry, 'Alas!' over all the evil abominations of the house of Israel, for they will fall by the sword, by famine, and by plague.
Whoever is far away will die of plague; whoever is near will fall by the sword; and whoever remains and is spared will die of famine. So I will spend my fury on them.

And you will know that I am Yahweh when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree and every leafy oak—wherever they offered soothing aromas to all their idols.
I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah,{c} in all their settlements. Then they will know that I am Yahweh."

notes.text: Local hilltop shrines used for worship, often of other gods.
Hebrew gillulim, a contemptuous word for idols, perhaps "dung-gods"; it occurs some forty times in Ezekiel.
The location of Diblah is unknown. Many scholars read Riblah, a town in Syria, since the Hebrew letters d and r look very similar.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"You, son of man—this is what the Lord Yahweh says to the land of Israel:{a} An end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.
Now the end is upon you. I will unleash my anger against you, judge you by your ways, and hold all your abominations against you.
My eye will not spare you, and I will have no pity. I will repay you for your ways, and your abominations will remain in your midst. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
"This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Disaster! A unique disaster—look, it is coming!
An end has come; the end has come. It has roused itself against you—look, it is coming!
Your doom{b} has come to you, inhabitant of the land. The time has come; the day is near—a day of panic, not of joyful shouting on the mountains.
Soon I will pour my wrath upon you; I will bring my anger to its full against you. I will judge you according to your ways and hold all your abominations against you.
My eye will not spare, and I will have no pity. I will repay you for your ways, and your abominations will remain in your midst. Then you will know that it is I, Yahweh, who strike.
"Look, the day! Look, it is coming! Your doom has gone out; the rod has blossomed, arrogance has budded.
Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. None of them will be left—none of their crowd, none of their wealth, nothing of distinction among them.{c}
The time has come; the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice or the seller mourn, for wrath is upon all its throng.

The seller will not return to what was sold as long as both of them live, for the vision concerns all its throng; it will not be revoked. Because of their guilt, not one of them will preserve his life.{d}
"They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to battle, for my wrath is upon all its throng.
The sword is outside; plague and famine are inside. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city will be devoured by famine and plague.
Even if their survivors escape, they will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each for his guilt.
Every hand will hang limp, and every knee will run with water.{e}
They will put on sackcloth, and horror will cover them. Shame will be on every face and baldness on every head.

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will become a thing unclean. Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to save them on the day of Yahweh's fury. They will not fill their appetites or their bellies with it, for it was the stumbling block of their guilt.
Their beautiful ornaments they turned to pride, and from them they made the images of their abominations and their detestable things. That is why I am making it unclean to them.
I will give it as plunder into the hands of strangers and as booty to the wicked of the earth, who will profane it.
I will avert my face from them as they profane my treasured place. Robbers will come into it and profane it.
"Forge a chain,{f} for the land is full of bloody crimes and the city is full of violence.
I will bring in the most evil of the nations, and they will seize their houses. I will end the pride of the mighty, and their sanctuaries will be profaned.
Anguish is coming! They will look for peace, and there will be no peace.
Calamity will follow calamity and rumor will follow rumor. They will seek a vision from a prophet, but instruction will perish from the priest and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, and the prince will be clothed in desolation; the hands of the common people will shake. I will treat them as their ways deserve and judge them by their own judgments. Then they will know that I am Yahweh."

notes.text: The Greek arranges vv. 3–9 in a different order and in a shorter form.
Hebrew tsephirah, a word of uncertain meaning; also in v. 10. Others render "turn" or "crown."
The Hebrew of v. 11 is obscure.
The Hebrew of v. 13 is difficult; "will preserve his life" may also be rendered "will strengthen himself."
That is, they will wet themselves with fear.
The meaning of this phrase is uncertain; the Greek lacks it.

verses.text: In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month (in August–September),{a} I was sitting in my house, and the elders of Judah were seated in front of me, when the hand of the Lord Yahweh fell on me there.
I looked, and there was a figure that looked like fire.{b} From what appeared to be his waist downward was fire, and from his waist upward was something like a brilliant shining, like gleaming metal.

He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my hair. The Spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the idol of jealousy, which provokes jealousy, was set up.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the valley.
Then he said to me, "Son of man, raise your eyes northward." So I raised my eyes northward, and there it was: north of the gate of the altar, at its entrance, stood this idol of jealousy.

He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing—the great abominations that the house of Israel is committing here, to drive me far from my sanctuary? But you will see still greater abominations."
Next he led me to the doorway of the court, and as I looked I saw a hole in the wall.
"Son of man," he said, "break through the wall." I broke through the wall, and I found a door.
He said to me, "Go in and see the evil abominations they are committing here."
I entered and looked: engraved over the whole wall were figures of every sort of crawling creature and detestable animal, together with all the idols of the house of Israel.

In front of them stood seventy of the elders of the house of Israel, and Jaazaniah{c} son of Shaphan{d} stood in their midst. Every man held a censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense was going up.

He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what the elders of the house of Israel do in darkness, every one of them in his chamber of carved images? They are saying, 'Yahweh does not see us; Yahweh has abandoned the land.'"
He said to me further, "You will yet see them committing abominations greater still."
Then he took me to the doorway of the gate of Yahweh's house on the north side, and women were sitting there weeping for Tammuz.{e}
He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? You will see still greater abominations than these."

Then he brought me into the inner court of the house of Yahweh, and there at the entrance of the temple of Yahweh, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men with their backs to the temple of Yahweh and their faces toward the east. They were bowing down eastward to the sun.

He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? Is it not enough for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they are committing here, that they must also fill the land with violence and provoke me again and again? Look, they are putting the branch to their nose!{f}
Therefore I will act in fury. My eye will not spare, and I will have no pity. Though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not listen to them."

notes.text: Hebrew: "in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month," counting from the spring new year; this was the month later called Elul, in 592 BC. The Greek has "the fifth month" (July–August).
Hebrew esh, "fire"; the Greek reads ish, "a man," which many scholars prefer (compare 1:27).
Jaazaniah means "Yahweh listens."
Shaphan means "rock badger" (hyrax). He was probably the royal secretary under Josiah (2 Kgs 22:3), whose family supported Jeremiah.
Tammuz (Sumerian Dumuzi) was a Mesopotamian god of fertility whose death was mourned each summer; the fourth month of the later Jewish calendar (June–July) is named after him.
The meaning of this expression is uncertain; it apparently describes a pagan ritual gesture or an insult. Jewish tradition reads "to my nose," one of the "corrections of the scribes."

verses.text: Then he called out in my hearing with a loud voice, "Bring near those appointed to punish the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand."

Then six men came by way of the upper gate that looks northward, each gripping his weapon of destruction. Among them was a man in linen clothing, with a scribe's writing kit at his side. They entered and stood next to the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel had risen from above the cherub,{a} where it had been, and moved to the threshold of the house. He called to the man dressed in linen with the writing kit at his side,
and Yahweh told him, "Pass through the city, all through Jerusalem, and mark{b} the foreheads of the people who sigh and groan over all the abominations done within it."
To the others he said in my hearing, "Go through the city after him and strike. Do not let your eye spare, and have no pity.

Old man, youth, and maiden, little ones and women—slay them all, to utter destruction. But do not come near anyone who bears the mark. Start at my sanctuary." So they started with the elders standing in front of the temple.
He said to them, "Defile the house and fill the courts with the slain. Go!" So they went out and struck people down throughout the city.
While they struck the people down and I was left by myself, I threw myself facedown and cried, "Ah, Lord Yahweh! Will you wipe out the whole remnant of Israel in pouring out your fury on Jerusalem?"

He said to me, "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is immense. The land is full of bloodshed and the city full of perversion of justice, for they say, 'Yahweh has abandoned the land; Yahweh does not see.'
As for me, my eye will not spare, and I will have no pity; I will bring their conduct down on their own heads."
Then the man in linen clothing, the writing kit at his side, brought his report: "I have done just as you ordered me."

notes.text: Cherubim were winged heavenly beings, often guardians of holy places (Gen 3:24); here, probably the cherubim of the ark in the Most Holy Place.
Hebrew taw, the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet, which in the script of the time was written like an X or a cross.

verses.text: Then I looked, and above the vault over the heads of the cherubim there appeared something like lapis lazuli, in form like a throne.

He said to the man dressed in linen, "Go in among the whirling wheels{a} beneath the cherubim. Take a double handful of the fiery coals from between the cherubim and throw them across the city." I watched him go in.
The cherubim were standing on the south side of the house when the man went in, and the cloud filled the inner court.
The glory of Yahweh rose from the cherub to the threshold of the house; the house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of Yahweh's glory.
The noise of the wings of the cherubim carried all the way to the outer court, like the voice of El Shaddai{b} speaking.
When he commanded the man clothed in linen, "Take fire from between the wheels, from between the cherubim," the man went in and stood beside a wheel.
One of the cherubim reached out his hand from between the cherubim to the fire that was among them, took some, and put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who took it and went out.
Something shaped like a human hand could be seen beneath the wings of the cherubim.
I looked, and there were four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub; the wheels looked like the gleam of a chrysolite stone.
As for their appearance, all four had the same form, as if one wheel were inside another.
When they moved, they could go in any of their four directions without turning as they went; wherever the head faced, they followed without turning as they went.
Their whole bodies—backs, hands, and wings—and the wheels too were covered with eyes all around; the four of them had their wheels.
As for the wheels, I heard them called "the whirling wheels."{c}
Each one had four faces: the first was the face of the cherub, the second a human face, the third a lion's face, and the fourth an eagle's face.{d}
Then the cherubim rose up. They were the same living creatures I had seen at the Chebar canal.
As the cherubim went, the wheels went at their side; and as the cherubim lifted their wings to mount up from the earth, the wheels too stayed with them and did not turn away.
When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still; when they rose, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creature was in them.
Then the glory of Yahweh went out from the threshold of the house and stopped above the cherubim.

As I watched, the cherubim lifted their wings and rose up from the earth, and the wheels went out alongside them. They halted at the entry of the east gate of Yahweh's house, and above them was the glory of the God of Israel.
They were the same living creatures I had seen under the God of Israel at the Chebar canal; and I recognized that they were cherubim.
Every one had four faces and four wings, and something like human hands was under their wings.
As for the form of their faces, they were the same faces whose appearance I had seen by the Chebar canal. Each one went straight ahead.

notes.text: Or "whirling wheels" (Hebrew galgal); also in vv. 6 and 13.
El Shaddai is traditionally "God Almighty"; the original meaning of Shaddai is uncertain.
Hebrew galgal, a word suggesting whirling or rolling.
Verse 14 is not found in the Greek. Compare 1:10, where the face of an ox stands in place of "the face of the cherub."

verses.text: The Spirit then raised me and brought me to the east-facing gate of Yahweh's house. At the gate's entrance were twenty-five men, and I saw among them two leaders of the people, Jaazaniah son of Azzur{a} and Pelatiah{b} son of Benaiah.{c}
He said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who devise wickedness and give evil counsel in this city.
They say, 'Is not the time near to build houses? This city is the pot, and we are the meat.'{d}
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man."
Then the Spirit of Yahweh fell upon me, and he told me, "Say, 'This is what Yahweh says: That is what you are saying, house of Israel; I know the thoughts that rise in your mind.
You have multiplied your slain in this city and filled its streets with the dead.
Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: The bodies you have laid in its midst are the meat, and this city is the pot; but you I will bring out of it.
You have feared the sword, and the sword is what I will bring upon you, declares the Lord Yahweh.
I will bring you out of the city, hand you over to foreigners, and carry out judgments against you.
You will fall by the sword; I will judge you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
This city will not be your pot, nor will you be the meat in it; I will judge you at the border of Israel.
Then you will know that I am Yahweh, whose statutes you have not walked in and whose judgments you have not carried out; instead, you have acted by the standards of the nations around you.'"{e}
While I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell facedown and cried out with a loud voice, "Ah, Lord Yahweh! Will you put a complete end to the remnant of Israel?"
The word of Yahweh came to me:

"Son of man, your brothers—your own brothers, your relatives,{f} and the whole house of Israel, all of them—are the ones of whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said, 'Keep far from Yahweh; this land was given to us as our possession.'

"So say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Though I drove them far away among the nations and scattered them through the lands, I have been a sanctuary to them for a little while{g} in the lands to which they have come.'
"Therefore say, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says: I will gather you from the peoples, assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and give you the land of Israel.'
They will come there and clear out of it all its vile things and all its abominations.
I will give them one heart{h} and put a new spirit within them. I will take the heart of stone out of their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they may walk in my statutes, keep my judgments, and carry them out. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God.
But those whose hearts follow the desire of their vile things and abominations—I will repay their deeds on their own heads, declares the Lord Yahweh."
Then the cherubim lifted their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was above them.
The glory of Yahweh went up from the midst of the city and stopped over the mountain east of the city.{i}
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me in the vision, by the Spirit of God, to the exiles in Chaldea. Then the vision I had seen left me,
and I told the exiles everything Yahweh had shown me.

notes.text: Azzur means "helper"; this Jaazaniah is a different man from the one in 8:11.
Pelatiah means "Yahweh rescues," which gives point to the question in v. 13.
Benaiah means "Yahweh has built."
Or "The time is not near to build houses." The image of the pot suggests the leaders saw themselves as the choice meat, safe inside the city.
Verses 11–12 are not found in the Greek.
Hebrew: "the men of your redemption," that is, relatives with the right and duty to redeem family property (Lev 25:25). The Greek has "the men of your captivity."
Or "I have been to them a sanctuary in small measure."
Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Greek have "another heart"; others render "an undivided heart."
That is, the Mount of Olives.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, you live among a rebellious house, people who have eyes for seeing yet see nothing and ears for hearing yet hear nothing, because they are a house of rebels.

"So you, son of man, pack an exile's baggage, and go into exile by day while they watch. Go as an exile from your place to another place as they watch; perhaps they will understand, though they are a rebellious house.
Bring out your baggage by day as they watch, like baggage for exile; then in the evening go out yourself as they watch, like those who go into exile.
While they watch, dig through the wall and carry the baggage out through it.
With them watching, hoist it onto your shoulder and take it out at dusk. Hide your face so that you do not look at the land, because I have made you an omen to the house of Israel."

I did just as I was commanded. By day I brought out my baggage as though for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hands. I carried it out in the darkness, lifting it onto my shoulder as they watched.
In the morning the word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, asked you, 'What are you doing?'
Say to them, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says: This oracle{a} concerns the prince in Jerusalem and the whole house of Israel who are in it.'
Say, 'I am a sign for you. As I have done, so it will be done to them; they will go into exile, into captivity.'
The prince among them will hoist his baggage onto his shoulder at dusk and leave; they will break through the wall to get him out. He will hide his face so that his eyes do not see the land.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he will not see it, and there he will die.{b}
Everyone around him, his helpers and all his troops, I will scatter to every wind, and I will unsheathe a sword after them.
Then they will know that I am Yahweh, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them through the countries.
But I will spare a few of them from the sword, from famine, and from plague, so that among the nations where they go they may recount all their abominations. Then they will know that I am Yahweh."
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, eat your bread with trembling, and drink your water with shuddering and anxiety.

Then say to the people of the land, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says about the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the land of Israel: They will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dismay, for their land will be stripped of all it contains because of the violence of all who live in it.
The inhabited towns will be laid waste, and the land will become a desolation. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, what is this proverb you have in the land of Israel: 'The days drag on, and every vision comes to nothing'?

So tell them, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: I will end this saying, and it will never again be heard on the lips of Israel.' Instead tell them, 'The days are at hand, and with them the substance of every vision.
No more will there be empty visions or smooth-tongued divination among the people of Israel.

For I am Yahweh. I will speak whatever word I speak, and it will be carried out without further delay. In your days, rebellious house, I will speak the word and carry it out, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, the house of Israel is saying, 'The vision he sees is for many days from now; he prophesies about distant times.'
So tell them, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Not one of my words will be postponed again. The word I speak will be done, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"

notes.text: Hebrew massa, "burden" or "oracle," a play on the baggage (also something carried) and on the "prince" (nasi, "one lifted up").
Zedekiah was blinded before he was taken to Babylon (2 Kgs 25:7).

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying. Say to those who prophesy out of their own imagination, 'Hear the word of Yahweh!
This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Woe to the foolish prophets who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing!
Your prophets, Israel, have been like jackals among ruins.
You have not gone up into the breaches or built up a wall around the house of Israel, so that it might stand firm in battle on the day of Yahweh.
Their visions are empty and their divining a lie. "Yahweh's declaration," they announce, though Yahweh never sent them; and still they wait for him to make their word come true.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken a lying divination when you say, "Yahweh declares," though I have not spoken?
"'Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you have spoken falsehood and seen lies, I am against you, declares the Lord Yahweh.

My hand will come down on the prophets whose visions are empty and whose divinations are lies. In the circle of my people they will have no seat; in the roll of Israel's house they will not be written; into Israel's land they will not come. And you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.
"'Because—yes, because—they have led my people astray, saying, "Peace," when there is no peace, and when someone builds a flimsy wall, they coat it with whitewash,
tell those who coat it with whitewash that it will fall. Torrential rain will come; you, great hailstones, will fall; and a storm wind will burst out.
When the wall has fallen, will people not ask you, "Where is the whitewash you coated it with?"
"'Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: In my fury I will make a storm wind burst out; in my anger there will be torrential rain, and in my fury hailstones to destroy.
I will tear down the wall you coated with whitewash and level it to the ground, so that its foundation is laid bare. When it falls, you will perish within it. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
So I will spend my fury on the wall and on those who coated it with whitewash, and I will say to you, "The wall is gone, and so are those who coated it—
those prophets of Israel who prophesied to Jerusalem and beheld for her visions of peace, though peace there was none, declares the Lord Yahweh."'
"As for you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own imagination. Prophesy against them

and say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Woe to you women who stitch magic bands{a} on every wrist and fashion veils for heads of every size, to trap souls! Will you trap the souls of my people and preserve souls for yourselves?

You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and scraps of bread, putting to death people who should not die and keeping alive people who should not live, by lying to my people, who listen to lies.

"'Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I am against your magic bands with which you hunt lives as if they were birds. I will tear them from your arms and set free the lives you hunt like birds.
I will rip away your veils and snatch my people out of your grip; never again will they be a catch in your hands. And you will know that I am Yahweh.

Because you have disheartened the righteous with lies, when I had not caused them grief, and have strengthened the hands of the wicked so that they do not turn from their evil way and save their lives,
so your empty visions and your divining are finished. I will snatch my people out of your grip, and you will know that I am Yahweh.'"

notes.text: The meaning of the Hebrew words for "bands" and "veils" is uncertain; they were evidently objects used in magic or divination.

verses.text: Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.
Then the word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their hearts and put the stumbling block of their guilt right before their faces. Should I let them consult me at all?

Therefore speak to them and tell them, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Any one of the house of Israel who sets up his idols in his heart and puts the stumbling block of his guilt before his face, and then comes to the prophet—I, Yahweh, will answer him myself, as his many idols deserve,
so that I may seize the house of Israel by their own hearts, since through their idols they have all become estranged from me.'
"So say to Israel's house, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Come back! Turn from your idols; turn your faces from every abomination of yours.

For when any one of the house of Israel, or any foreigner residing in Israel, separates himself from me, sets up his idols in his heart, puts the stumbling block of his guilt before his face, and then comes to a prophet to consult me for himself, I, Yahweh, will answer him myself.
I will set my face against that man and make him a sign and a byword, and I will cut him off from among my people. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
"'If the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, I, Yahweh, have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand against him and wipe him out from among my people Israel.
They will bear their guilt; the guilt of the prophet will be the same as the guilt of the one who consults him,

so that the house of Israel will stray from me no more and no longer make themselves unclean with all their rebellions. They will be a people to me, and I will be God to them, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, if a land sins against me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out my hand against it, break its supply of bread, send famine on it, and cut off from it both people and animals,
if these three men were living there—Noah, Daniel,{a} and Job—their righteousness would rescue themselves alone, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"If I let wild beasts roam through the land and they leave it childless, so that it becomes a desolation that no one passes through because of the beasts,
as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, even if these three men were in it, they could not save sons or daughters. They alone would be saved, and the land would become a desolation.
"Or suppose I bring a sword on that country and command, 'Sword, go through the land!' and cut away from it human and beast alike;
as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, even if these three men were in it, they could not save sons or daughters; they alone would be saved.
"Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out my fury on it in bloodshed, to cut off from it both people and animals,
as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, should Noah, Daniel, and Job be living there, not a son and not a daughter would they rescue. Their righteousness would rescue themselves alone.

"For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: How much worse will it be when I send my four dreadful judgments against Jerusalem—sword, famine, wild beasts, and plague—to cut off from it both people and animals!

But look, a remnant will be left in it, a band of escapees—sons and daughters led out. They will come out to you, and when you see their ways and their doings, you will be comforted over the evil I brought on Jerusalem, over all that I brought on it.
They will console you when you see their conduct and their deeds, for you will know that it was not without cause that I did all I did in it, declares the Lord Yahweh."

notes.text: The Hebrew spelling is Danel (as also in 28:3), the name of a righteous ancient hero known from texts found at Ugarit; Jewish tradition identifies him with the Daniel of the book of Daniel. The name means "God is my judge."

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, what makes the vine's wood any better than wood from other trees—the vine shoot that was among the forest trees?
Is wood ever taken from it to make anything useful? Do people make a peg from it to hang any utensil on?
No, it is thrown into the fire for fuel. When the fire has consumed both its ends and its middle is charred, is it good for anything?
Look, while it was still whole nothing was made from it. How much less, once fire has eaten it and it is scorched, will anything be made from it!
"Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I will give up the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will set my face against them. Though they have escaped the fire, the fire will still consume them. And you will know that I am Yahweh when I set my face against them.
I will make the land a desolation, because they have acted unfaithfully, declares the Lord Yahweh."
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, confront Jerusalem with her abominations
and say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this to Jerusalem: Your roots and your birthplace are in Canaan's land. An Amorite was your father, and a Hittite your mother.{a}
As for your birth, on the day you were born your cord was not cut, you were not washed in water to cleanse you, you were not rubbed with salt or wrapped in cloths.
No eye pitied you enough to do any of these things for you out of compassion. Instead, you were thrown out into the open field, because you were despised on the day you were born.
"'And I passed by you and saw you thrashing in your own blood. In your blood I told you, "Live!" Yes, in your blood I told you, "Live!"{b}
I let you multiply like the sprouts of the field. You grew and grew tall and came to the fullest beauty;{c} your breasts took shape and your hair grew long, yet you were naked and exposed.

"'I passed by you again and saw you, and you were at the age for love. So I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness. I swore an oath to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord Yahweh, and you became mine.
I bathed you in water, rinsed your blood from you, and rubbed you with oil.
I clothed you with embroidered cloth, gave you sandals of fine leather,{d} wrapped you in fine linen, and covered you with silk.
I decked you out in ornaments: bangles for your arms, a chain for your neck,
a ring in your nose, earrings in your ears, and a splendid crown on your head.
So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was fine linen, silk, and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey, and oil. You became exceedingly beautiful and rose to royalty.
Among the nations word of you went out because of your beauty, flawless as it was through the splendor I had put on you, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"'But you trusted in your beauty and used your fame to play the prostitute. You lavished your favors on anyone who passed by; your beauty became his.{e}
You took some of your garments and made for yourself colorful high places, and there you played the prostitute—such things should never come about or happen.
You also took your beautiful jewelry of my gold and my silver, which I had given you, and made for yourself male images, and with them you played the prostitute.
You took your embroidered garments to cover them, and you set my oil and my incense before them.
The food I gave you—the fine flour, oil, and honey with which I fed you—you set before them as a soothing aroma. That is what happened, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"'And you took your sons and your daughters, children you had borne to me, and slaughtered them as food for those images. Was your whoring such a small thing?
You slaughtered my children and gave them up, making them pass through the fire to the images.
In all your abominations and prostitution you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood.
"'After all your wickedness—woe, woe to you, declares the Lord Yahweh—
you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty shrine in every square.
At the head of every street you built your lofty shrine and made your beauty an abomination. You spread your legs to everyone who passed by and multiplied your prostitution.
You prostituted yourself with the Egyptians, your lustful neighbors,{f} and multiplied your prostitution to provoke me.
So I stretched out my hand against you, cut back your allotted portion, and handed you over to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct.
You also prostituted yourself with the Assyrians, because you were not satisfied; you played the prostitute with them, and still you were not satisfied.
Then you multiplied your prostitution with the land of merchants, Chaldea,{g} and even with this you were not satisfied.
"'How feverish{h} your heart is, declares the Lord Yahweh, when you do all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute!
When you built your mound at the head of every street and made your lofty shrine in every square, you were not like a prostitute, because you scorned payment.
Adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!
Every prostitute is paid, yet you handed out payment to every lover of yours; you bribed them to come in to you from all around for your prostitution.
So you were the opposite of other women in your prostitution: no one chased after you to play the prostitute. You paid a fee instead of receiving one; you were the opposite.
"'Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of Yahweh.

This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because your lust{i} was poured out and your nakedness exposed in your prostitution with your lovers, and because of all your abominable idols and the blood of your children that you gave to them,

that is why I am gathering every lover with whom you took pleasure, everyone you loved and everyone you hated. From all around I will gather them against you; I will uncover your nakedness before them, and they will look on all of it.
I will judge you as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and I will bring on you the blood of fury and jealousy.

I will give you into their hands; your mound they will pull down and your lofty shrines they will break apart. They will peel off your clothing and carry away your fine jewels, and they will leave you naked and exposed.
They will bring up a mob against you, stone you, and hack you to pieces with their swords.
They will burn your houses and carry out judgments on you in the sight of many women. I will stop you from playing the prostitute, and you will no longer pay fees.
Then my fury against you will be spent, my jealousy will depart from you, and I will grow quiet and be angry no more.

You did not bear in mind the time of your youth; you raged at me with all of this. So now I am bringing your ways back on your head, declares the Lord Yahweh. Did you not add this lewdness to all your abominations?
"'Look, everyone who quotes proverbs will quote this one about you: "Like mother, like daughter."

You are your mother's daughter, who loathed her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, who lives with her daughters to your north,{j} and your younger sister, who lives to your south, is Sodom with her daughters.
Not content to follow in their ways and do their abominations, you soon became, as if that were a trifle, more depraved than they in all you did.
As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, Sodom your sister and her daughters did not do what you have done, you and your daughters.
See, this was the guilt of Sodom your sister: pride, a surplus of bread, and untroubled ease were hers and her daughters', yet the hand of the poor and needy they did not strengthen.
They grew lofty and did abomination before me, so I took them away, as you have seen.{k}
Samaria's sins were not half of yours. Your abominations outnumber hers, and by all you have done you have made your sisters look righteous.

You also must carry your shame, since you have pleaded your sisters' case. Your sins were so much more abominable than theirs that they look more righteous than you. Be ashamed, then, and carry your shame, because you have made your sisters look righteous.
"'Yet I will turn back their captivity—Sodom's and her daughters', Samaria's and her daughters'—and yours too in their midst,
that you may carry your shame and blush for everything you did, becoming a comfort to them.
Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, Samaria and her daughters, will be restored to what they were before, and you and your daughters will be restored to what you were before.
In your proud days you would not so much as mention your sister Sodom,

before your wickedness was uncovered? Now you have become like her, an object of scorn for the daughters of Edom{l} and all those around her, and for the daughters of the Philistines—all around you who despise you.
Your lewdness and your abominations—you carry them, declares Yahweh.
"'For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I will deal with you as you have done, you who have despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish an everlasting covenant with you.
You will recall your ways and be humiliated when you take in your sisters, those older and those younger than you. I will give them to you as daughters, though not by your covenant.
I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am Yahweh,
so that you remember and feel shame, and because of your humiliation never open your mouth again, when I forgive you for all you did, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"

notes.text: The Amorites and Hittites were among the peoples living in Canaan before Israel (Gen 15:19–21); the point is that Jerusalem's origins were pagan.
The Greek lacks the repeated sentence "I said to you as you lay in your blood, 'Live!'"
The Hebrew is uncertain; it may mean "you came to have the finest ornaments."
Hebrew tahash, a fine leather of uncertain kind, perhaps from dolphins or sea cows.
The Hebrew phrase "your beauty became his" is uncertain.
Hebrew: "great of flesh," a sexual euphemism.
Or "Chaldea, the land of merchants." Hebrew: "the land of Canaan, Chaldea"; "Canaan" here means "merchants."
Or "weak"; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
Hebrew nechosheth, perhaps "copper" (that is, money) or "lust"; the meaning is uncertain.
Hebrew: "on your left"; the right and left referred to south and north for someone facing east.
Or "as you have seen."
So some ancient witnesses; the main Hebrew text and the Greek have "Aram" (Syria). In Hebrew the two names differ by one similar letter.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, pose a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel.

Say, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
A great eagle with great wings, long pinions,
and full plumage of many colors
came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.

He plucked off its topmost shoot,
carried it to a land of trade,
and set it in a city of merchants.

It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height;
its branches turned toward him,
and its roots stayed beneath him.
So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots.

"'Then came a second great eagle,
broad of wing and thick with feathers.
And see, this vine twisted its roots toward him
and sent its tendrils reaching to him,
away from the bed where it grew,
for him to water it.

It had been planted in good soil beside abundant waters,
so that it could produce branches and bear fruit
and become a magnificent vine.'

"Say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Will it prosper? Will its roots not be torn out and its fruit stripped away, until every new leaf it puts forth dries up? No mighty arm, no crowd of people, will be needed to wrench it up by the roots.
Look—it is replanted; will it prosper? Once the east wind touches it, will it not dry up entirely, dry up in the very bed where it sprouted?'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:

"Say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not know what these things mean?' Tell them, 'The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and its officials, and brought them to himself in Babylon.{b}
He took one of royal descent{c} and cut a covenant with him, binding him by a curse-oath. The land's men of power he carried away,
so that the kingdom would be kept low and not lift itself up, but would survive by keeping his covenant.

But that king revolted against him, sending his messengers down to Egypt for horses and a host of troops. Will he prosper? Will a man who does these things get away? He has broken the covenant—will he get away?
"'As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, in the place of the king who enthroned him, whose curse-oath he scorned and whose covenant he broke—with him, in the middle of Babylon, he will die.
Pharaoh, for all his great force and vast assembly, will do nothing for him in the battle, when the siege mound is heaped up and the siege tower built for cutting down many souls.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. He gave his hand in pledge and yet did all these things; he will not escape.
"'So the Lord Yahweh says this: As I live, my curse-oath that he scorned and my covenant that he broke—I will lay them on his head.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for the unfaithfulness he committed against me.
All the picked men{d} in all his ranks will go down by the sword, and those who are left will be scattered to all the winds. And you will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken.'

"This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
I myself will take a shoot from the lofty top of the cedar and set it out;
I will pluck a tender twig from its topmost shoots
and plant it myself on a high and towering mountain.

On Israel's lofty mountain I will plant it;
it will put out branches and bear fruit
and become a majestic cedar.
Every kind of winged creature will dwell beneath it,
sheltering in the shade of its boughs.

Then all the trees of the field will know
that I, Yahweh, bring low the high tree
and make the low tree tall,
dry up the green tree
and make the dry tree flourish.
I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do it."

notes.text: The Hebrew word rendered "willow" is uncertain.
This was Nebuchadnezzar's deportation of King Jehoiachin in 597 BC (2 Kgs 24:10–17).
That is, Zedekiah (2 Kgs 24:17).
So some ancient witnesses; the main Hebrew text has "fugitives."

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:

"What do you mean, you who keep quoting this saying concerning Israel's land:
'The fathers eat unripe grapes,
and it is the children's teeth that go numb'?
As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, you will no longer use this proverb in Israel.
Look, all souls are mine. As the father's soul is mine, so the son's soul is mine. The soul that sins—that soul shall die.
"Take a man who is righteous, who practices justice and right.

On the mountains he does not feast at shrines; he does not raise his eyes to the idols of Israel's house. His neighbor's wife he does not defile, and he does not come near a woman in her time of impurity.
He wrongs no one; the pledge he took for a debt he gives back. He seizes nothing by robbery; his bread he gives to the hungry, and the naked he clothes with a garment.
He does not lend at interest or take a profit. He keeps his hand from wrongdoing and judges fairly between one person and another.
He walks in my statutes and keeps my judgments, acting faithfully. Such a man is righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"Now let him father a son who is a robber, one who sheds blood and does any one of these things
(though the father did none of them): he eats at the mountain shrines, defiles his neighbor's wife,
oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not return the pledge, lifts his eyes to the idols, commits abomination,
lends at interest, and takes a profit. Will he live? He will not live. Because he has done all these abominations, he will surely be put to death; his blood will be on his own head.
"But now let this man father a son who observes all the sins his father has done; he observes them and does nothing like them.
On the mountains he does not feast at shrines; he does not raise his eyes to the idols of Israel's house. His neighbor's wife he does not defile.
He wrongs no one; he holds back no pledge and seizes nothing by robbery. His bread he gives to the hungry, and the naked he clothes with a garment.
He holds back his hand from the poor,{a} takes neither interest nor increase, does my judgments, and follows my statutes. He shall not die because of his father's guilt; he shall surely live.
His father, since he extorted and robbed a brother and did what was evil among his own people—look, he shall die in his guilt.
"Yet you ask, 'Why does the son not bear the guilt of his father?' When the son has done what is just and right and has kept all my statutes and carried them out, he will surely live.

The soul that sins—that soul shall die. A son shall not carry his father's guilt, and a father shall not carry his son's guilt. On the righteous rests his own righteousness, and on the wicked rests his own wickedness.
"But should the wicked man turn back from all the sins he did, guard all my statutes, and practice justice and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die.
None of the transgressions he has committed will be remembered against him; because of the righteousness he has practiced, he will live.
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked, declares the Lord Yahweh? Would I not rather that he turn from his ways and live?

But if a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, committing the same abominations the wicked person commits, will he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done will be remembered. For the unfaithfulness he has practiced and the sin he has committed, for these he will die.
"Still you say, 'The Lord's way does not measure up.' Hear now, house of Israel: Does my way not measure up? Is it not rather your ways that fail to measure up?
When a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die for it; for the wrong he has done he will die.
And once the wicked man turns back from the wickedness he did and practices justice and right, he will keep his soul alive.
Because he considered and turned away from all the transgressions he had committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
Yet the house of Israel says, 'The Lord's way is not fair.' Are my ways unfair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are unfair?
"Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, declares the Lord Yahweh. Repent and turn away from all your transgressions, so that guilt will not be your downfall.
Cast away from you every rebellion of yours that you have done, and make for yourselves a heart that is new and a spirit that is new. Why will you die, house of Israel?
For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone, declares the Lord Yahweh. So turn, and live!"

notes.text: So the main Hebrew text; the Greek has "from injustice" (compare v. 8).

verses.text: "And you—raise a dirge over Israel's princes,

and say:
'What a lioness your mother was among the lions!
She lay down among young lions;
she reared her cubs.

"'When she saw that her hope was lost,
that what she had waited for had come to nothing,
she took another of her cubs
and made him a young lion.

He knew their strongholds{b}
and laid waste their towns.
The land and all that filled it were appalled
at the sound of his roaring.

Then the nations set against him
the provinces on every side.
They spread their net over him;
he was caught in their pit.

With hooks they put him in a cage
and brought him to the king of Babylon.{c}
They brought him into fortresses
so that his voice would no longer be heard
on the mountains of Israel.

"'Your mother was like a vine in your vineyard,{d}
planted beside the waters.
It was fruitful and full of branches
because of abundant water.

It had strong branches,
fit for rulers' scepters.
It towered high
among the thick foliage;
it was conspicuous for its height
and its many branches.

Now it is planted in the wilderness,
in a dry and thirsty land.

Fire has gone out from its main branch
and consumed its shoots and fruit,
so that it has no strong branch left,
no scepter for ruling.'
This is a lament, and it has become a lament."

notes.text: This was King Jehoahaz, taken to Egypt by Pharaoh Neco in 609 BC (2 Kgs 23:31–34).
Hebrew: "He knew his widows"; a slight change gives "he broke down their strongholds" or "he ravaged their widows."
Probably King Jehoiachin (2 Kgs 24:8–15) or Zedekiah (2 Kgs 25:7).
Hebrew: "in your blood"; the text is uncertain, and many scholars emend it to "in a vineyard."

verses.text: In the seventh year, on the tenth day of the fifth month (in July–August),{a} some of the elders of Israel came to consult Yahweh, and they sat down before me.
Then the word of Yahweh came to me:

"Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and tell them, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Have you come to consult me? As I live, I will not let myself be consulted by you, declares the Lord Yahweh.'
"Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Then make known to them the abominations of their ancestors.

Tell them, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: On the day I chose Israel, I lifted my hand in oath to the seed of Jacob's house, and in Egypt's land I made myself known to them. I lifted my hand to them, saying, "I am Yahweh your God."
That day I lifted my hand to them, swearing to lead them out of Egypt's land to a land I had scouted for them, one flowing with milk and honey, the jewel of every land.
And I said to them, "Each of you, throw away the detestable things your eyes feast on, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God."

"'They rebelled against me and would not hear me. Not one cast away the vile things that held his eyes, and Egypt's idols they did not abandon. So I spoke of pouring my fury on them, of exhausting my anger on them right there in Egypt's land.
Yet I acted for my name's sake, to keep it from being profaned before the nations they lived among, before whose eyes I had revealed myself to them by leading them out of Egypt's land.
So out of Egypt's land I led them, and I brought them to the wilderness.
I gave them my statutes and made known to them my judgments, by which a person who carries them out will live.
My Sabbaths too I gave them, to be a sign between me and them, for knowing that I am Yahweh who sets them apart as holy.

"'But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness. They did not walk in my statutes, and they rejected my judgments, by which a person who carries them out will live, and they utterly profaned my Sabbaths. So I resolved to pour out my fury on them in the wilderness to wipe them out.
Yet I acted for my name's sake, to keep it from being profaned before the nations, in whose view I had led them out.
And I, too, lifted my hand to them in the wilderness, swearing not to bring them into the land I had given, the land flowing with milk and honey, the jewel of every land,
because they rejected my judgments, did not walk in my statutes, and profaned my Sabbaths; for their hearts went after their idols.
But my eye took pity on them, and I held back from destroying them; I did not make a full end of them in the wilderness.
"'I said to their children in the wilderness, "Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers or keep their judgments or defile yourselves with their idols.
I am Yahweh your God. Walk in my statutes, keep my judgments, and carry them out.
Keep my Sabbaths holy, so that they will be a sign between me and you, and you will know that I am Yahweh your God."

"'But the children rebelled against me. They did not walk in my statutes or keep my judgments and carry them out—by which a person who carries them out will live—and they profaned my Sabbaths. So I resolved to pour out my fury on them and spend my anger against them in the wilderness.
Yet I drew back my hand and acted for my name's sake, to keep it from being profaned before the nations in whose view I had led them out.
Moreover, I raised my hand in an oath to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the countries,
because they had not carried out my judgments but had rejected my statutes and profaned my Sabbaths, and their eyes were fixed on their fathers' idols.
So I gave them statutes that were not good and judgments by which they could not live.
I made them unclean by their own gifts, as they made every firstborn pass through the fire,{b} that I might appall them, and that they might know that I am Yahweh.'
"Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and tell them, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says: In this also your ancestors blasphemed me by acting unfaithfully toward me.

For I brought them into the land that I had lifted my hand to give them, and wherever they saw a lofty hill or a leafy tree, they slaughtered their sacrifices there, there they set their offerings that provoked me, there they laid their soothing aromas, and there they poured out their drink offerings.
So I said to them, "What is this high place you go to?" And it is called Bamah{c} to this day.'
"Therefore say to the house of Israel, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Will you defile yourselves in the way your ancestors did, and prostitute yourselves after their detestable things?

When you offer your gifts and make your sons pass through the fire, you are defiling yourselves with all your idols to this day. Should I let myself be consulted by you, house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I will not let myself be consulted by you.
What you have in mind will never happen—when you say, "Let us be like the nations, like the clans of the countries, serving wood and stone."
"'As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured fury I will rule as king over you.
I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the countries where you are scattered, with a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, and outpoured fury.
I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
As I entered into judgment with your ancestors in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Lord Yahweh.
I will make you pass under the rod and bring you into the bond of the covenant.{d}
I will sift out from you the rebels and those who revolt against me. From the land where they sojourn I will lead them out, but Israel's soil they shall not enter. And you will know that I am Yahweh.

"'And you, house of Israel, the Lord Yahweh says this: Go, every one of you, serve his idols! But afterward—surely you will listen to me, and my holy name you will profane no more with your gifts and idols.

For it is on my holy mountain, on Israel's lofty mountain, declares the Lord Yahweh, that the entire house of Israel will serve me, all of it in the land. There I will welcome them with pleasure, and there I will ask for your contributions, the first and best of your gifts, and all your holy things.

Like a soothing aroma I will welcome you with pleasure when I lead you out of the peoples and collect you from the lands of your scattering; and through you I will show myself holy before the nations' eyes.
Then you will know that I am Yahweh, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land I raised my hand in an oath to give to your ancestors.
There you will remember your ways and all the deeds by which you defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have done.
You will know that I am Yahweh when I deal with you for the sake of my name, not according to your evil ways or your corrupt deeds, house of Israel, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:{e}
"Son of man, set your face toward the south. Preach against the south and prophesy against the forest of the Negev.{f}

Say to the forest of the Negev, 'Hear Yahweh's word. The Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am setting a fire in you; every tree in you, green or dry, it will devour. The fierce flame will not be put out, and from the Negev to the north every face will be seared by it.
All flesh will see that I, Yahweh, have kindled it; it will not be quenched.'"
Then I said, "Ah, Lord Yahweh! They are saying of me, 'Is he not just a maker of parables?'"

notes.text: Hebrew: "in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month," counting from the spring new year; this was the month later called Av, in 591 BC. The Greek has only "on the fifteenth of the month."
Or "when they offered up every firstborn"; compare 16:21.
Bamah means "high place." Ezekiel plays on the sound of the question "What (mah) is the high place to which you go (ba'im)?"
The Greek has "and I will bring you in by number"; the meaning of the Hebrew word rendered "bond" is uncertain.
In Hebrew, 20:45–49 is numbered 21:1–5, and 21:1–32 is numbered 21:6–37.
The Negev is the dry region south of Judah; "south" here also represents Judah and Jerusalem (21:2).

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem and preach against the sanctuaries. Prophesy against the land of Israel
