and say to Israel's land, 'Yahweh says this: Look, I am coming at you. My sword I will draw out of its sheath, and from you I will cut away righteous and wicked alike.
Because I am going to cut off from you both righteous and wicked, my sword will go out of its sheath against all flesh from south to north.
Then all flesh will know that I, Yahweh, have drawn my sword from its sheath; it will not return to it again.'
"As for you, son of man, groan! Groan before their eyes with breaking heart{a} and bitter grief.

When they ask you, 'Why are you groaning?' say, 'Because of the news that is coming. Every heart will melt, every hand go limp, every spirit grow faint, and every knee run with water. Look, it is coming, and it will happen, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:

"Son of man, prophesy and say, 'This is what my Lord says: Say:
A sword, a sword is sharpened
and also polished—

He has handed it over for burnishing,
for the palm to grip;
sharpened is this sword, burnished too,
to be placed in the killer's hand.'
Shout and howl, son of man, for this sword is for my people, for every prince of Israel; they are tossed to it together with my people. So slap your thigh.{c}
For a testing has come—and what if the scepter that despises is no more? declares the Lord Yahweh.{d}

"As for you, son of man, prophesy, and clap your hands together.
Let the sword strike twice, even three times—
a sword for the slain,
the sword for the great slaughter
that surrounds them,

Cut hard to the right!
Turn and strike to the left,
wherever your blade is aimed.

I too will clap my hands together
and satisfy my fury.
I, Yahweh, have spoken."
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"As for you, son of man, mark out two roads for the sword of the king of Babylon to take, both starting from the same land. Make a signpost and put it at the head of the road to a city.
Mark out a road for the sword to come to Rabbah of the Ammonites, and another to Judah, to fortified Jerusalem.
For Babylon's king has halted where the road parts, where the two ways begin, to seek an omen. He rattles the arrows, inquires of the household gods,{f} and examines a liver.

Into his right hand comes the lot for Jerusalem: to set up battering rams, to open the mouth for slaughter, to raise the battle cry, to set battering rams against the gates, to heap up a ramp, and to build a siege wall.
To those who have sworn solemn oaths,{g} it will seem a false divination; but he will bring their guilt to remembrance, so that they will be captured.

"Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you have brought your guilt to remembrance by your open transgressions, so that your sins appear in all your deeds—because you have come to remembrance—you will be taken in hand.
And you, defiled and wicked one, Israel's prince, your day has arrived, the hour when guilt reaches its end,
the Lord Yahweh says this: Take off the turban; lift away the crown! This will not stay this way. Raise up what is low; pull down what is high.
A ruin, a ruin, a ruin I will make it! This too will not happen until he comes to whom judgment belongs, and I will give it to him.{h}

"And you, son of man, prophesy and say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this about the Ammonites and their scorn:
A sword! A sword unsheathed for the slaughter,
burnished to devour, to gleam like a lightning bolt—

while they divine emptiness for you
and see lying omens for you—
to place you on the necks of the slain, the wicked,
whose day has arrived,
the hour when guilt reaches its end.

Return it to its sheath!
In the place where you were created,
in the land of your origin, I will judge you.

I will pour out my indignation on you;
I will blow on you with the fire of my wrath.
I will hand you over to brutal men,
skilled in destruction.

You will be fuel for the fire;
your blood will be in the midst of the land.
You will not be remembered,
for I, Yahweh, have spoken.'"

notes.text: Hebrew: "with breaking of loins."
The Hebrew of this line is very obscure, and any rendering is a guess.
A gesture of grief or alarm (Jer 31:19).
The Hebrew of v. 13 is very obscure.
The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered "slaughter" here is uncertain.
Hebrew teraphim, figurines used in divination (Gen 31:19).
The meaning of the Hebrew phrase is uncertain; it may refer to the oaths of loyalty sworn to the king of Babylon.
Or "until he comes whose right it is." The wording echoes Gen 49:10.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"As for you, son of man, will you judge? Will you judge the city of bloodshed? Then confront her with all her abominations.
Say, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says: A city that sheds blood in her midst so that her time comes, and that makes idols for herself to defile herself!

You have become guilty by the blood you have shed and defiled by the idols you have made. You have brought your days near and arrived at the end of your years. Therefore I have made you a reproach to the nations and a mockery to all the countries.
Those near and those far from you will mock you, you of defiled name, full of turmoil.
"'Look, the princes of Israel within you, each according to his power, have been bent on shedding blood.
In you they have treated father and mother with contempt; in your midst they have oppressed the foreigner; in you they have wronged the fatherless and the widow.
You have despised my holy things and profaned my Sabbaths.
Men who peddle slander to spill blood are in you; men who feast at mountain shrines are in you; lewdness they practice in your midst.
A father's nakedness is uncovered{a} in you; a woman unclean in her impurity is forced in you.
With his neighbor's wife one man does abomination; another defiles his daughter-in-law by lewdness; another in you forces his sister, his father's daughter.
In you they take bribes to shed blood. You take interest and profit and extort gain from your neighbors by oppression. And you have forgotten me, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"'So look, I clap my hands over the profit you have plundered and over the blood that is shed within you.
Will your courage endure, or your hands stay strong, in the days when I deal with you? I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do it.
I will scatter you among the nations and disperse you through the countries, and I will purge your uncleanness from you.
You will be profaned{b} through your own doing in the sight of the nations. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, the house of Israel has become dross to me. All of them are copper, tin, iron, and lead inside a furnace; they are the dross of silver.
Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because all of you have become dross, I am going to gather you into the middle of Jerusalem.
As people gather silver, copper, iron, lead, and tin into a furnace to blow fire on it and melt it, so I will gather you in my anger and fury, put you inside, and melt you.
I will gather you and blow on you with the fire of my wrath, and you will be melted within the city.
As silver is melted in a furnace, so you will be melted inside it. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, have poured out my fury on you."
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, say to her, 'You are a land that has not been cleansed or rained upon in the day of indignation.'
There is a conspiracy of her prophets{c} within her, like a roaring lion tearing its prey. They devour lives, seize treasure and precious things, and multiply the widows within her.

Her priests wrong my teaching and treat my holy things as profane. Between sacred and common they draw no line; the difference between unclean and clean they never make known. From my Sabbaths they hide their eyes, and among them I am made profane.
Her officials within her are like wolves tearing prey, shedding blood and destroying lives to get unjust gain.
Her prophets daub whitewash over all of it, seeing empty visions and divining lies, and declaring, 'The Lord Yahweh says this,' though Yahweh never spoke.
The common people have extorted and robbed; the poor and the needy they have mistreated, and the foreigner they have wronged without justice.
I looked among them for one man to repair the wall, to take his stand before me in the gap for the land so that I would not wreck it—and there was none.
So I have poured out my indignation on them; I have consumed them with the fire of my wrath. I have brought their conduct down on their own heads, declares the Lord Yahweh."

notes.text: That is, they have sexual relations with their fathers' wives (Lev 18:8).
So the main Hebrew text. The Greek reads differently ("I will give inheritances in you").
The Greek has "her princes," which many scholars prefer since prophets are treated in v. 28.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother.
They became prostitutes in Egypt; they played the prostitute in their youth. There their breasts were fondled, and there their virgin nipples were caressed.
The elder bore the name Oholah,{a} her sister the name Oholibah.{b} They became mine and gave birth to sons and daughters. Their names stand for this: Oholah is Samaria, and Oholibah is Jerusalem.
"Oholah went whoring though she was mine. She burned with desire for her lovers, for Assyria's warriors{c}
clothed in blue, governors and commanders, all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses.
She bestowed her prostitution on them, all of them the elite of Assyria, and she defiled herself with all the idols of everyone she lusted after.
She did not give up the prostitution she had practiced since Egypt, for in her youth men had lain with her, caressed her virgin nipples, and poured out their lust on her.
So I gave her over into her lovers' hands, into the hands of the Assyrians she burned for.
They exposed her nakedness, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became a byword among women, and judgments were carried out on her.
"Her sister Oholibah saw this, yet in her lust she was more corrupt than her sister, and her prostitution exceeded her sister's.
She lusted after the Assyrians—governors and commanders, warriors clothed in splendor, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men.
I saw that she too was defiled; the two of them went one road.
But she carried her prostitution further. She saw men carved on the wall, images of Chaldeans engraved in vermilion,
with belts around their waists and flowing turbans on their heads, all of them looking like officers, a portrait of Babylonians whose native land was Chaldea.
As soon as she saw them, she lusted after them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.
Babylon's sons came in to her, to the bed of love, and made her unclean with their whoring; and when they had defiled her, she pulled herself away from them in revulsion.
When she flaunted her prostitution and exposed her nakedness, I turned from her in disgust, just as I had turned from her sister.
Yet she multiplied her prostitution, remembering the days of her youth when she played the prostitute in the land of Egypt.
She burned for her lovers there, men with flesh like a donkey's flesh and an issue like a stallion's issue.
So you longed for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians caressed your nipples and fondled your young breasts.{d}
"So, Oholibah, the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am rousing against you the lovers from whom you pulled away in revulsion; from all around I will bring them against you—

Babylon's sons and every Chaldean, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa,{e} and with them all Assyria's sons—handsome young men every one, governors and prefects, captains and summoned men, every one mounted on horses.

They will come against you with weapons,{f} chariots, and wagons, and with a horde of peoples. They will set themselves against you on every side with large shield, small shield, and helmet. I will hand judgment over to them, and they will judge you by their own standards.

I will direct my jealousy against you, and they will deal with you in fury. They will cut off your nose and your ears, and the rest of you will fall by the sword. They will take your sons and daughters, and the rest of you will be consumed by fire.
They will strip you of your clothes and take away your beautiful jewelry.
So I will put an end to your lewdness and the prostitution you brought from the land of Egypt. You will not lift your eyes to them or remember Egypt anymore.
"For the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am giving you into the hands of the ones you hate, the ones from whom you pulled away in revulsion.
They will deal with you in hatred, take away everything you have worked for, and leave you naked and bare. The nakedness of your prostitution will be exposed, and your lewdness and prostitution.
These things will be done to you because you prostituted yourself with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.
Your sister's road you have walked, so her cup I will set in your hand.

"This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
You will drink your sister's cup,
deep and wide;
it will bring scorn and derision,
for it holds so much.

You will drink it and drain it,
gnaw its broken pieces,
and tear your breasts.
For I have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you have forgotten me and thrown me behind your back, you must bear the penalty of your lewdness and your prostitution."
Yahweh said to me, "Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then declare to them their abominations.

For they have committed adultery, and there is blood on their hands. They have committed adultery with their idols; they have even made the children they bore to me pass through the fire to them as food.
Moreover, they have done this to me: on that same day they defiled my sanctuary and profaned my Sabbaths.
For when they had slaughtered their children for their idols, on that same day they came into my sanctuary to profane it. That is what they did in the middle of my house.
"They even sent for men coming from far away; a messenger was sent to them, and they came. For them you bathed, painted your eyes, and adorned yourself with jewelry.
On a magnificent couch you sat, a table laid out in front of it, and on it you placed my incense and my oil.
The sound of a carefree crowd was around her, with men of the common sort brought in, drunkards{g} from the wilderness. They put bracelets on the women's wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.
Then I said of her who was worn out by adulteries, 'Now they will commit prostitution with her, even her!'
And they went in to her as one goes in to a prostitute. So they went in to Oholah and to Oholibah, the lewd women.
But righteous men will judge them with the sentence for adulteresses and the sentence for women who shed blood, because they are adulteresses and there is blood on their hands.
"For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Bring up an assembly against them, and hand them over to terror and plunder.
The assembly will pelt them with stones and hack them with swords; their sons and daughters will be killed and their houses burned down.
So I will put an end to lewdness in the land, and all women will take warning and not imitate your lewdness.
Your lewdness will be repaid on you, and you will bear the penalty for your sins with idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh."

notes.text: Oholah means "her tent," perhaps alluding to Samaria's own shrines.
Oholibah means "my tent is in her," alluding to Yahweh's temple in Jerusalem.
Or "neighbors"; the Hebrew word can mean "near."
The Hebrew of this line is difficult; "the Egyptians" is implied from v. 19.
Pekod, Shoa, and Koa were peoples east of the Tigris; the names may also be wordplays on Hebrew words for "punishment" and "cry for help." The Greek has "Phacuc, Sue, and Hychue."
The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered "weapons" is uncertain.
Or "Sabeans," following the written Hebrew text; the meaning is uncertain.

verses.text: In the ninth year, on the tenth day of the tenth month (in December–January),{a} the word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, record for yourself the date, this very day. On this exact day Babylon's king has closed in on Jerusalem.

For her blood remains inside her;
on bare rock she set it.
She never spilled it on the soil
where dust might hide it.

To stir up fury, to take vengeance,
I have put her blood on the bare rock,
so that it would not be covered.

"'Therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says:
Woe to the city of bloodshed!
I too will make the pile great.

Pile up the wood, light the fire,
boil the meat through,
stir in the spices,{e}
and let the bones burn.

Then set the empty pot on the coals,
so that it grows hot and its copper glows,
its impurity melts within it,
and its corrosion is consumed.
Your uncleanness is lewdness. I sought to make you clean, yet clean of your impurity you would not be; and clean you will not be again till I have brought my fury on you to rest.
I, Yahweh, have spoken. It is coming, and I will do it. I will not hold back; I will not spare or relent. You will be judged according to your ways and your deeds, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, I am about to take from you with a single blow the delight of your eyes. Yet you must not mourn or weep or let your tears flow.
Sigh, but silently; hold no mourning rites for the dead. Wrap your turban on and lace your sandals onto your feet. Leave your mustache uncovered, and do not eat the bread men bring to mourners."{g}
I spoke to the people at dawn; at dusk my wife died. And at dawn I did what I had been ordered to do.
Then the people said to me, "Won't you explain to us what these actions of yours have to do with us?"
I said to them, "The word of Yahweh came to me:

'Say to the house of Israel, "This is what the Lord Yahweh says: I am about to profane my sanctuary, the pride of your strength, the delight of your eyes, and the longing of your soul. The sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword.
You will do as I have done: you will not cover your upper lip or eat the bread of mourners.
Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet. You will not mourn or weep, but you will waste away because of your guilt and groan to one another.
Ezekiel will be a sign to you; you will do everything he has done. When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh."'
"And you, son of man—on the day when I take away their fortress, their glorious joy, what delights their eyes and what their souls long for, their sons and their daughters—
on that day a fugitive will come to you to bring the news to your ears.
On that day your mouth will be opened to the fugitive; you will speak and no longer be mute. So you will be a sign to them, and they will know that I am Yahweh."

notes.text: Hebrew: "in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month," counting from the spring new year; this was the month later called Tevet, in January 588 BC by the usual reckoning (2 Kgs 25:1).
Or "logs"; compare v. 10.
Or "rust" or "scum"; the meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain; also in vv. 11–12.
That is, no portion is set aside to be spared.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain; others render "pour out the broth."
The Hebrew of this line is uncertain.
Hebrew: "the bread of men"; many scholars, with a slight change, read "the bread of mourners"; also in v. 22.

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"Son of man, set your face toward the Ammonites{a} and prophesy against them.

Say to the Ammonites, 'Hear the word of the Lord Yahweh. This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you said "Aha!" over my sanctuary when it was profaned, over the land of Israel when it was laid waste, and over the house of Judah when they went into exile,
so look, I am giving you to the sons of the east to own. They will set their camps in you and place their dwellings among you; they will be the ones to eat your fruit and drink your milk.
Rabbah I will turn into a grazing ground for camels, and Ammon's towns into a fold for sheep. And you will know that I am Yahweh.
For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because you clapped your hands and stamped your feet and rejoiced with all the contempt of your heart against the land of Israel,

therefore I have stretched out my hand against you and will give you as plunder to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and wipe you out from the countries; I will destroy you. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.'
"This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because Moab and Seir{b} said, 'Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations,'
therefore I am going to lay open the flank of Moab, stripping it of its towns, its frontier towns, the glory of the land—Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.{c}
Together with Ammon I will give it to the sons of the east to own, that Ammon may not be remembered among the nations.
And I will carry out judgments on Moab. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.
"The Lord Yahweh says this: Since Edom took vengeance on Judah's house and became deeply guilty by avenging itself on them,

therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I will stretch out my hand against Edom and cut off from it both people and animals. I will make it a ruin; from Teman to Dedan{d} they will fall by the sword.
I will take my vengeance on Edom by the hand of my people Israel, and they will deal with Edom according to my anger and my fury. Then they will know my vengeance, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"This is what the Lord Yahweh says: Because the Philistines acted in vengeance and took revenge with contempt of heart, seeking to destroy with undying hostility,
therefore this is what the Lord Yahweh says: I am going to stretch out my hand against the Philistines. I will cut off the Cherethites{e} and destroy the rest of the seacoast.
I will carry out great vengeance on them with furious rebukes. Then they will know that I am Yahweh, when I lay my vengeance on them."

notes.text: The Ammonites lived east of the Jordan; their capital was Rabbah (modern Amman).
Seir is the mountain region of Edom. The Greek lacks "and Seir."
Beth-jeshimoth means "house of the wastelands"; Baal-meon, "lord of the dwelling"; Kiriathaim, "double city."
Teman was a region of Edom; Dedan was an Arabian oasis to the southeast.
The Cherethites were a people associated with the Philistines, perhaps from Crete; the name plays on the verb "cut off" (karath).

verses.text: It was in the eleventh year, on the first of the month,{a} that Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, since Tyre{b} has said about Jerusalem, 'Ha! She that was the door of the peoples is shattered; she has been flung open to me. Now that she is wasted, I will grow full,'
the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am coming at you, Tyre. Many nations I will bring up against you, as the sea heaves up its breakers.
They will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers. I will scrape her soil from her and make her a bare rock.
She will become a place in the middle of the sea for spreading out fishing nets, for I have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh. She will become plunder for the nations,
and her daughters{c} on the mainland will be killed by the sword. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.
"For the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, out of the north I am bringing Nebuchadrezzar{d} of Babylon against Tyre, king of kings, with horse and chariot, cavalry and a vast mob of troops.
He will kill your daughters on the mainland with the sword. He will build a siege wall against you, heap up a ramp against you, and raise a wall of shields against you.
His battering rams he will set against your walls, and your towers he will tear down with his iron tools.
So countless are his horses that their dust will bury you. At the din of cavalry, wheels, and chariots your walls will quake, when he comes in at your gates as men come into a city broken open.
His horses' hoofs will tread every street of yours. Your people he will slay with the sword, and your strong pillars will crash down to the earth.

Your riches will be seized and your goods carried off as plunder. Your walls will be pulled down and your pleasant houses wrecked; your stones, your timbers, and your rubble will be dumped into the sea.
I will hush the clamor of your songs; the music of your lyres will never sound again.
I will make you a bare rock; you will be a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I, Yahweh, have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"This is what the Lord Yahweh says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands shake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and slaughter is done within you?

Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. They will clothe themselves with trembling and sit on the ground, trembling every moment and appalled at you.

They will raise a dirge for you and say to you:
'Ah, how you are lost,
you who were peopled from the seas,
the city held in honor,
strong upon the sea,
she and those who dwelt in her,
who laid their dread
on all her inhabitants!

Now the islands shake
on the day you fall;
the islands out in the sea
are terrified at your departure.'
"For this is what the Lord Yahweh says: When I make you a desolate city, like cities that are no longer inhabited, when I bring up the deep over you and the vast waters cover you,

then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit,{e} to the people of long ago. I will make you live in the land below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not be inhabited or take your place{f} in the land of the living.
I will make you a horror, and you will be no more. Though you are sought, you will never be found again, declares the Lord Yahweh."

notes.text: The month is not given in the Hebrew or the Greek. The eleventh year of Jehoiachin's exile was 587/586 BC, the year Jerusalem fell (v. 2).
Tyre means "rock." It was the great Phoenician port, built largely on an island off the coast of modern Lebanon.
That is, its dependent settlements; also in v. 8.
Hebrew Nebuchadrezzar, a form closer to the Babylonian Nabu-kudurri-usur, "Nabu, protect my heir." His siege of Tyre lasted thirteen years (compare 29:18).
That is, the realm of the dead.
So the Greek ("nor stand"); the Hebrew has "and I will give glory."

verses.text: The word of Yahweh came to me:
"As for you, son of man, take up a lament over Tyre.

Say to Tyre, who sits at the gateways of the sea, merchant of the peoples to many coastlands, 'This is what the Lord Yahweh says:
Tyre, you have said,
"I am perfect in beauty."

Your borders were in the heart of the seas;
your builders perfected your beauty.

They fashioned all your planks
of juniper from Senir;{a}
they took a cedar from Lebanon
to make a mast for you.

The people of Sidon and Arvad{e} were your rowers;
your skilled men, Tyre, were aboard as your sailors.

Gebal's{f} elders and its experts were in you,
mending your leaks.
Every seagoing ship and its crews
came to you to deal in your wares.
"'Persia, Lud, and Put{g} were in your army as your men of war. They hung shield and helmet in you; they gave you splendor.
Men of Arvad and your army were on your walls all around, and men of Gammad{h} were in your towers. They hung their shields on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.
"'Tarshish{i} traded with you because of your great abundance of every kind of wealth; for your wares they gave silver, iron, tin, and lead.
Javan,{j} Tubal, and Meshech{k} were your dealers; for your wares they paid in human lives and in bronze utensils.
From Beth-togarmah{l} they gave horses, war horses, and mules for your wares.
The people of Dedan{m} traded with you; many coastlands were your markets. They paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
Aram{n} traded with you because of your many products; for your wares they gave turquoise, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies.
Judah and the land of Israel traded with you; for your merchandise they gave wheat from Minnith, millet,{o} honey, oil, and balm.
Damascus traded with you because of your many products and your great abundance of every kind of wealth, with wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.{p}
Vedan and Javan from Uzal{q} gave wrought iron, cassia, and calamus for your wares.
Dedan traded with you in saddlecloths for riding.
Arabia and all the princes of Kedar{r} were your customers; in lambs, rams, and goats they traded with you.
The merchants of Sheba and Raamah{s} traded with you; for your wares they gave the finest of all spices, every kind of precious stone, and gold.
Haran, Canneh, Eden, the merchants of Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad{t} traded with you.
They traded with you in choice garments, in cloaks of blue and embroidered work, and in carpets of many colors, bound with twisted cords, in your marketplace.

The ships of Tarshish carried your merchandise.
So you were filled and heavily loaded
in the heart of the seas.

"'Your rowers have brought you
out into the vast waters.
The east wind has shattered you
in the heart of the seas.

Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise,
your sailors and your seamen,
your caulkers, your dealers in merchandise,
and all your men of war who are in you,
with all the company that is in your midst,
will sink into the heart of the seas
on the day of your downfall.

At the sound of your sailors' cry
the open lands{u} will shake.

All who handle the oar
will come down from their ships;
the seamen and all the sailors of the sea
will stand on the shore.

Over you they will shout aloud
and wail with bitter cries;
dust they will toss on their heads,
and in ashes they will wallow.

In their wailing they will take up a lament for you
and chant over you:
"Who was like Tyre,
like her now silenced{w} in the midst of the sea?"

When your wares came out from the seas,
you satisfied many peoples;
with your great wealth and merchandise
you enriched the kings of the earth.

Now you are shattered by the seas,
in the depths of the waters;
your merchandise and all your company
have sunk with you.

notes.text: Senir is another name for Mount Hermon (Deut 3:9).
Hebrew bath-ashurim, traditionally "daughter of Assyrians"; with a different division of the letters, "in cypress" (bitashurim).
Kittim is Cyprus, named after the city of Kition; the term was later used of western coastlands generally.
Elishah is probably Alashiya, an ancient name for Cyprus or part of it.
Arvad was a Phoenician island city north of Tyre.
Gebal is Byblos, a Phoenician port north of Sidon.
Lud is probably Lydia in Asia Minor; Put is probably Libya.
The identity of Gammad is unknown; the Greek has "guards."
Tarshish was a distant western port, probably in Spain (Tartessus); the Greek has "Carthaginians."
Javan is Greece (Ionia).
Tubal and Meshech were peoples of central Asia Minor (compare 38:2).
Beth-togarmah was a region probably in eastern Asia Minor (Armenia).
So the main Hebrew text; the Greek has "Rhodians," reflecting a reading "Rodan."
Some ancient witnesses read "Edom"; in Hebrew the two names differ by one similar letter.
The meaning of the Hebrew word rendered "millet" (pannag) is uncertain.
Or "white wool."
The Hebrew of v. 19 is uncertain; "from Uzal" may instead be read as part of the list of goods.
Kedar was a tribe of the Arabian desert.
Sheba and Raamah were peoples of southern Arabia.
Chilmad is unidentified; the other names are trading centers of Mesopotamia and Arabia.
Or "the pasturelands"; the meaning is uncertain.
Verse 31 is not found in the Greek.
The Hebrew word is uncertain; some read "like a ruin" or "like her destroyed one."

verses.text: Yahweh's word came to me:

"Son of man, tell the ruler of Tyre, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: / Your heart has grown lofty, / and you have said, "A god am I; / in the seat of gods I sit, / in the heart of the seas." / Yet you are a mortal, not a god, / though you have made your mind like the mind of a god.
Look, you are wiser than Danel;{a} / no secret is too dark for you.
By your wisdom and your understanding / you have gained wealth for yourself, / and gold and silver you have amassed / in your treasure houses.
By your great skill in trade / you have multiplied your wealth, / and your heart has grown lofty / because of your wealth.
"'So the Lord Yahweh says this: / Since you have made your mind / like the mind of a god,
look, I am bringing foreigners against you, / the most ruthless of nations. / They will bare their swords against the beauty your wisdom made / and defile your splendor.
Down to the pit{b} they will send you, / and you will die the death of the slain / in the heart of the seas.

Before the one who slays you,
will you go on saying, "I am a god"?
You will be a mortal, not a god,
in the grip of those who pierce you.
You will die the death of the uncircumcised{c} / at the hand of foreigners. / For I have spoken, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, raise a dirge over the king of Tyre and say to him, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: / You were the seal of perfection,{d} / full of wisdom and flawless in beauty.

In Eden, God's garden, you lived;
gems of every kind adorned you:
carnelian, chrysolite, and moonstone,
beryl, onyx, and jasper,
lapis lazuli, turquoise, and emerald;{e}
and your settings and mountings were worked in gold.
On the day you were created they were made ready.
You were an anointed cherub, a guardian;{f} / I placed you there. / On God's holy mountain you were; / among stones of fire you walked about.
Blameless you were in your ways / from the day you were created, / until wrong was discovered in you.

Through the abundance of your trade / your insides filled with violence, / and you sinned. / So I banished you as profane from God's mountain, / and I destroyed you, guardian cherub, / from among the stones of fire.
Your heart grew lofty because of your beauty; / you ruined your wisdom for the sake of your splendor. / I hurled you to the earth; / before kings I set you out, / for them to feast their eyes on you.

By the mass of your guilt,
by the dishonesty of your trade,
you defiled your holy places.
So from within you I made a fire break out;
it devoured you,
and I turned you to ashes on the ground
before the eyes of all who watched you.
All among the peoples who knew you / are appalled at you. / You have become a terror, / and you will be no more forever.'"
Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, set your face toward Sidon{g} and prophesy against her.

Say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am coming against you, Sidon, and I will win glory in your midst. They will know that I am Yahweh when I carry out judgments on her and show myself holy in her.
I will send plague into her and blood into her streets. The slain will fall within her, by the sword that comes against her from every side. And they will know that I am Yahweh.
"'No more will the house of Israel have a briar that pricks or a thorn that wounds from any of the neighbors around them who treat them with contempt. And they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.

"'The Lord Yahweh says this: When I gather Israel's house from the peoples among whom they are scattered, and show myself holy through them before the nations' eyes, then they will live on their own soil, which I gave to my servant Jacob.

They will live on it in security, building houses and planting vineyards; in security they will live, when I carry out judgments on all their neighbors who treat them with contempt. And they will know that I am Yahweh their God.'"

notes.text: Hebrew Danel; see the note at 14:14.
That is, the realm of the dead.
That is, a shameful death without honorable burial; the phrase is used of the Phoenicians, who practiced circumcision, as a mark of disgrace.
The Hebrew phrase is obscure; it may mean "sealer of proportion," that is, the model of a perfect design. The Greek has "a seal of likeness."

The identification of many of these stones is uncertain. The Hebrew lists nine stones, all found among the twelve on the high priest's breastpiece (Exodus 28:17–20). The Greek lists all twelve of the breastpiece stones, adds silver and gold, and has a different final clause.
Or "You were with an anointed guardian cherub." The Hebrew pronoun "you" has an unusual feminine form; the Greek reads "with the cherub" and lacks "anointed."
Sidon, about 25 miles (40 kilometers) north of Tyre, was the other great Phoenician city.

verses.text: In the tenth year, on the twelfth day of the tenth month (in December–January),{a} Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, set your face against Pharaoh king of Egypt, and prophesy against him and against all Egypt.

Speak and say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: / Look, I am coming against you, / Pharaoh, king of Egypt, / the great monster{b} sprawled / in the midst of his Nile channels, / who says, "My Nile is mine; / I made it for myself."
I will set hooks in your jaws / and make the fish of your streams cling to your scales. / I will haul you up from the midst of your streams, / with every fish of your streams / stuck to your scales.

I will fling you into the wilderness, / you and all the fish of your streams. / On the open field you will fall; / no one will gather you up or collect you. / To the beasts of the earth and the birds of the sky / I have given you as food.
Then all who live in Egypt will know / that I am Yahweh, / because they have been a staff of reed / to the house of Israel.

When they took hold of you by the hand,{c} you splintered / and tore open every shoulder of theirs; / when they leaned their weight on you, you snapped, / and made every one of their hips give way.{d}
"'So the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am bringing a sword upon you, and I will cut off from you human and beast.
Egypt's land will become a desolation and a ruin, and they will know that I am Yahweh. Because he said, "The Nile is mine, and I made it,"
look, I am coming against you and against your streams. I will turn Egypt's land into an utter ruin, a desolation, from Migdol to Syene{e} and as far as the border of Cush.{f}
No human foot will cross it, and no animal's foot will cross it; for forty years it will be uninhabited.

I will make Egypt's land a desolation among desolate lands, and its cities will lie desolate among ruined cities for forty years. I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
"'Yet the Lord Yahweh says this: At the end of forty years I will gather the Egyptians from the peoples where they were scattered.
I will turn back Egypt's captivity and return them to Pathros,{g} their homeland, and they will be a lowly kingdom there.
It will be the lowliest of the kingdoms and will never again lift itself above the nations. I will make them so few that they will not rule over the nations.
Never again will Egypt be the trust of Israel's house; instead it will be a reminder of their guilt in turning to them for help. And they will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.'"
In the twenty-seventh year, on the first day of the first month (in March–April),{h} Yahweh's word came to me:

"Son of man, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon drove his army to hard labor against Tyre. Every head was rubbed bald and every shoulder rubbed raw. Yet from Tyre neither he nor his army got any wages for the labor he spent on it.

So the Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am giving Egypt's land to Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon. He will carry off its riches,{i} take its spoil, and seize its plunder, and that will be the wages for his army.
As payment for the work he labored at, I have given him Egypt's land, because they did it for me, declares the Lord Yahweh.
"On that day I will make a horn{j} sprout for Israel's house, and I will give you an open mouth among them. And they will know that I am Yahweh."

notes.text: Hebrew "in the tenth month, on the twelfth of the month." On the spring-start calendar used in Ezekiel, the tenth month is Tevet; the date falls in January 587 BC. The Greek reads "the twelfth year ... on the first of the month."
Hebrew tannim, a variant of tannin, "sea monster" or "dragon"; here a picture of the crocodile.
So the Hebrew margin and the Greek; the Hebrew text has "by your palm."
Probable reading; compare the Greek "crushed the loins of them all." The Hebrew reads "made all their hips stand."
Migdol was in the northeast of Egypt and Syene (modern Aswan) in the far south; the phrase means "from one end of Egypt to the other."
That is, the upper Nile region (Nubia, in modern Sudan).
That is, Upper (southern) Egypt.
Hebrew "in the first, on the first of the month." On the spring-start calendar the first month is Nisan; the date falls in April 571 BC, the latest dated oracle in the book.
Or "its multitude."
The horn is a symbol of strength.

verses.text: Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, prophesy and say, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: / Howl, "Alas for the day!"
For the day is near, / the day of Yahweh is near, / a day of cloud, / a time of doom for the nations.
A sword will come against Egypt, / and anguish will seize Cush, / when the slain fall in Egypt, / when her wealth is carried away / and her foundations torn down.
Cush, Put, and Lud, all the mixed peoples,{a} Cub,{b} and the people of the allied land{c} will fall by the sword with them.

"'Yahweh says this:
Egypt's supporters will fall,
and her proud strength will come down.
From Migdol all the way to Syene
the sword will cut them down within her,
declares the Lord Yahweh.
They will be desolate / among desolate lands, / and its cities will lie / among ruined cities.
They will know that I am Yahweh / when I set fire to Egypt / and all her helpers are crushed.
"'On that day messengers will go out from me in ships to terrify unsuspecting Cush. Anguish will take hold of them on Egypt's day—for look, it is coming!
"'The Lord Yahweh says this: / I will put an end to Egypt's horde / by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon.
He and his people with him, / the most ruthless of nations, / will be brought in to ruin the land. / They will bare their swords against Egypt / and fill the land with the slain.

I will turn the Nile channels into dry ground / and sell the land into the hands of evil men. / By the hand of foreigners I will make desolate / the land and everything in it. / I, Yahweh, have spoken.
I will make Pathros desolate, / set fire to Zoan,{e} / and carry out judgments on Thebes.{f}
I will pour out my fury on Pelusium,{g} / Egypt's stronghold, / and cut off the horde of Thebes.

At Tehaphnehes{l} the day will grow dark{m} / when I break the yokes of Egypt there / and her proud strength comes to an end in her. / A cloud will cover her, / and her daughters will go into captivity.
So I will carry out judgments on Egypt, / and they will know that I am Yahweh.'"
In the eleventh year, on the seventh day of the first month (in March–April),{n} Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Look, it has not been bound up for healing; no bandage has been put on to strengthen it so that it can grasp a sword.
So the Lord Yahweh says this: I am coming against Pharaoh king of Egypt. I will shatter his arms, the sound one as well as the broken one, and make the sword drop from his hand.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands.
I will strengthen the arms of Babylon's king and put my sword in his hand, but I will break Pharaoh's arms, and he will groan before him with the groans of a mortally wounded man.

I will strengthen the arms of Babylon's king, while Pharaoh's arms will drop. They will know that I am Yahweh when I put my sword into the hand of Babylon's king and he stretches it out against Egypt's land.
I will scatter the Egyptians among the nations and disperse them through the lands. And they will know that I am Yahweh."

notes.text: Or "all Arabia"; the Hebrew consonants can be read either way. The Greek list differs (it has "Persians, and Cretans, and Lydians, and Libyans, and all the mixed multitude").
Cub is otherwise unknown; many scholars read Lub, "Libya."
Hebrew "the children of the land of the covenant"; the Greek has "the children of my covenant." The phrase may refer to allies of Egypt, or possibly to Judeans living in Egypt.
Hebrew Noph, the ancient capital of Lower Egypt, near modern Cairo; also in v. 16. Instead of "the idols," the Greek has "the nobles."
Zoan, called Tanis by the Greeks, was in the northeastern Nile delta.
Hebrew No, the great city of Upper Egypt, modern Luxor; also in vv. 15–16.
Hebrew Sin; also in v. 16. Pelusium was a frontier fortress in the northeastern delta. The Greek has "Sais" here and "Syene" in v. 16.
The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain; the Greek reads "and waters will be poured out."
Hebrew Aven ("wickedness"), a play on On, the city called Heliopolis, "city of the sun," northeast of modern Cairo.
Pi-beseth, called Bubastis by the Greeks, was in the eastern delta.
Hebrew "they"; the pronoun is feminine and probably refers to the towns. The Greek has "the women."
Tehaphnehes (also spelled Tahpanhes) is Daphnae, a fortress in the northeastern delta (compare Jeremiah 43:7–9).
So the Greek and some ancient witnesses; the main Hebrew text has "will hold back."
Hebrew "in the first, on the seventh of the month." On the spring-start calendar the first month is Nisan; the date falls in April 587 BC.

verses.text: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month (in May–June),{a} Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his horde: / 'Whom are you like in your greatness?
Consider Assyria,{b} a cedar in Lebanon, / with lovely boughs and shade like a forest's, / towering in height, / its crown up among the clouds.{c}
The waters made it great; / the deep made it tall, / sending its streams / all around the place it was planted / and sending its channels / to all the trees of the field.
So it grew taller / than all the trees of the field; / its boughs multiplied / and its branches grew long / from the abundant water as it spread out.
In its boughs / every bird of the sky made its nest; / under its branches / every beast of the field gave birth; / and in its shade / all the great nations lived.
It was beautiful in its greatness, / in the length of its limbs, / for its roots went down / to abundant waters.

The cedars in God's garden / could not rival it; / the junipers were nothing like its boughs, / and the plane trees{d} were nothing / to compare with its branches. / No tree in God's garden / matched it in beauty.
I made it beautiful / with its mass of limbs, / and all the trees of Eden, / those in God's garden, envied it.
"'So the Lord Yahweh says this: Because it{e} towered high and set its crown among the clouds, and its heart grew proud of its height,
I handed it over to the mightiest ruler of the nations, who will surely deal with it as its wickedness deserves. I have driven it out.

Foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and left it lying. On the mountains and in every valley its limbs have fallen; its branches lie broken in every ravine of the land. All the peoples of the earth came out from its shade and left it.
On its fallen trunk all the birds of the sky settle, / and among its branches / all the beasts of the field take shelter.

This is so that no trees by the waters may tower to such a height or set their crowns among the clouds, and that no well-watered trees{f} may rise to equal them. For every one of them is given over to death, to the world below, among mortals, with those who descend to the pit.

"'The Lord Yahweh says this: On the day it went down to Sheol{g} I made the deep mourn for it and covered it over;{h} I held back its streams, and the great waters were checked. For its sake I dressed Lebanon in mourning, and every tree of the field wilted over it.

At the sound of its fall I made the nations quake, when I cast it down to Sheol with those who descend to the pit. And all Eden's trees, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all that drink water, were comforted in the world below.
They too went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword—those who had been its arm,{i} who lived in its shade among the nations.

"'Whom are you like, then, in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden? Yet you too will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the world below. Among the uncircumcised you will lie, with the sword's slain. This is Pharaoh and all his horde, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"

notes.text: Hebrew "in the third, on the first of the month." On the spring-start calendar the third month is Sivan; the date falls in June 587 BC.

Some scholars, reading one letter differently, find here not "Assyria" but "a cypress" (te'ashshur), so that the cedar stands for Pharaoh himself. The Greek has "the Assyrian was a cypress in Lebanon."
So the Greek; the Hebrew word may mean "thick foliage"; also in vv. 10 and 14.
The identification of these trees is uncertain.
Hebrew "you"; the Hebrew shifts between "you" and "it."
Hebrew "all that drink water."
Sheol is the realm of the dead; also in vv. 16–17.
Or "I closed the deep over it." The Hebrew is difficult; the Greek has simply "the deep mourned for him."
The Hebrew is difficult; the Greek reads "his seed."

verses.text: In the twelfth year, on the first day of the twelfth month (in February–March),{a} Yahweh's word came to me:

"Son of man, raise a dirge over Pharaoh king of Egypt and say to him: / 'Among the nations you likened yourself to a young lion, / but you are like a monster in the seas; / you burst out in your rivers, / churned the waters with your feet, / and fouled their streams.
"'The Lord Yahweh says this: / I will cast my net over you / with a throng of many peoples, / and they will haul you up in my dragnet.
I will fling you onto the land; / on the open field I will hurl you down. / I will make every bird of the sky settle on you / and let the beasts of all the earth gorge themselves on you.
I will spread your flesh on the mountains / and fill the valleys with your carcass.{b}

I will water the land with what flows from you,
with your blood up to the mountains,
and the gullies will be full of you.

When I put out your light, I will veil the heavens
and blacken their stars;
a cloud will hide the sun,
and the moon will give no light.
Every shining light in the heavens / I will darken over you, / and I will set darkness over your land, / declares the Lord Yahweh.
"'I will trouble the hearts of many peoples / when I bring your shattering{c} among the nations, / to lands you have not known.

I will leave many peoples appalled at you; / their kings will shudder in horror over you / when I brandish my sword before their faces. / Each of them will tremble every moment for his own life / on the day of your fall.
"'For the Lord Yahweh says this: / The sword of Babylon's king / will come upon you.
By the swords of warriors / I will fell your horde— / the most ruthless of nations, every one. / They will ravage Egypt's pride, / and all her horde will be wiped out.
I will destroy all her cattle / from beside the abundant waters. / No human foot will churn them again, / and no hoof of beast will churn them.
Then I will let their waters settle / and make their streams flow like oil, / declares the Lord Yahweh.

When I make Egypt's land a desolation,
a land stripped of all that filled it,
when I strike down every one of its inhabitants,
then they will know that I am Yahweh.
This is a dirge, and they will chant it; / the daughters of the nations will chant it. / Over Egypt and over all her horde they will chant it, / declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
In the twelfth year, on the fifteenth day of the month,{d} Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, wail over Egypt's horde, and send it down—her and the daughters of mighty nations—to the world below, with those who go down to the pit.
'Are you lovelier than anyone? Down with you; lie among the uncircumcised!'{e}
They will fall among those slain by the sword. A sword has been handed over; drag her away with all her hordes.{f}
The mightiest of the warriors will speak to him from the midst of Sheol, along with his helpers: 'They have gone down; they lie still, the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.'
"Assyria is there with all her company, their graves all around it,{g} all of them slain, fallen by the sword.
Her graves are set in the remotest depths of the pit, and her company lies around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, they who once spread terror in the land of the living.

"Elam{h} is there with all her horde around her grave, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who went down uncircumcised to the world below, they who once spread terror in the land of the living. Now they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.

Among the slain they have made a bed for her with all her horde, their graves all around her, all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword. Because terror of them was spread in the land of the living, they bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit; she is laid among the slain.
"Meshech and Tubal{i} are there with all their horde, their graves all around them, all of them uncircumcised, pierced by the sword, because they spread terror in the land of the living.

And they do not lie with the fallen warriors of the uncircumcised,{j} who descended to Sheol in their battle gear, their swords placed beneath their heads and their shields{k} upon their bones, for the terror of these warriors was in the land of the living.
And you too will be broken among the uncircumcised and lie with those slain by the sword.
"Edom is there, her kings and all her chiefs, who for all their might are laid with those slain by the sword. With the uncircumcised they lie, and with those who descend to the pit.

"The princes of the north are there, all of them, and all the Sidonians, who went down with the slain in shame, despite the terror their might inspired. They lie uncircumcised with those slain by the sword and bear their disgrace with those who go down to the pit.
"Pharaoh will see them and be consoled over all his horde—Pharaoh and all his army, slain by the sword, declares the Lord Yahweh.
For I spread terror of him{l} in the land of the living, yet he will be laid among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword—Pharaoh and all his horde, declares the Lord Yahweh."

notes.text: Hebrew "in the twelfth month, on the first of the month." On the spring-start calendar the twelfth month is Adar; the date falls in March 585 BC. The Greek has "the tenth month."
Or "your heap of worms"; the Hebrew word is uncertain.
So the Hebrew; the Greek reads "your captivity."

The Hebrew does not name the month. If the twelfth month of v. 1 is meant, the date is in March 585 BC. The Greek reads "in the first month" (Nisan, in March–April), which would place the oracle in April 586 BC.
This verse is absent from the Greek, which has a differently arranged text in vv. 19–21.
The Hebrew of this verse is difficult.
Hebrew "him"; the Hebrew shifts between masculine and feminine references to Assyria in vv. 22–23.
Elam was a kingdom east of Babylon, in what is now southwestern Iran.
On Meshech and Tubal see the note at 27:13.
The Greek has "with the giants that fell of old," perhaps reading a slightly different Hebrew word for "of the uncircumcised."
Probable reading; the Hebrew has "their iniquities."
So the Hebrew text and the Greek; the Hebrew margin has "my terror."

verses.text: Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, speak to your people's children and tell them: Suppose I bring the sword against a land, and the people of that land pick one man from their ranks and make him their lookout.
He sees the sword coming against the land, sounds the ram's horn,{a} and warns the people.
Then if anyone hears the horn's blast and pays no heed, and the sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head.
He heard the horn's blast and paid no heed; his blood is on himself. Had he heeded, he would have saved his life.

But suppose the lookout sees the sword coming and does not sound the horn, so the people are not warned, and the sword comes and takes one of them. That person is taken away in his guilt, but I will hold the lookout to account for his blood.
"As for you, son of man, I have made you a lookout for Israel's house. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, warn them for me.

When I say to the wicked, 'Wicked one, you will surely die,' and you do not speak up to warn the wicked away from his course, that wicked person will die in his guilt, but his blood I will require from your hand.
But if you do warn the wicked to turn from his course, and he does not turn from it, he will die in his guilt, but you will have rescued your own life.
"And you, son of man, say to Israel's house: This is what you keep saying: 'Our rebellions and our sins weigh on us, and we are wasting away under them. How then can we live?'

Tell them: 'As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I take no delight in the death of the wicked, but rather in the wicked turning from his course and living. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why should you die, house of Israel?'

"And you, son of man, tell your people's children: A righteous person's righteousness will not rescue him on the day he rebels, and a wicked person's wickedness will not bring him down on the day he turns from it. The righteous will not be able to live by his righteousness on the day he sins.
If I tell the righteous that he will surely live, and he trusts in his own righteousness and does wrong, none of his righteous acts will be remembered; he will die for the wrong he has done.
And if I tell the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right—
if the wicked man returns a pledge, pays back what he stole, and walks in the statutes that give life, doing no wrong—he will surely live; he will not die.
Not one sin of his will be remembered against him. Justice and right are what he has done; he will surely live.
"Yet your people's children say, 'The Lord's way is not fair,' when it is their own way that is not fair.
When a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, he will die for it.
And if the wicked one leaves his wickedness behind and practices justice and right, by these he will live.
Yet you say, 'The Lord's way is not fair.' House of Israel, I will judge each of you by your ways."
In the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth day of the tenth month (in December–January),{b} someone who had fled from Jerusalem reached me with the news: "The city is struck down!"
Now the evening before the fugitive arrived, Yahweh's hand had come on me, and he opened my mouth before the man reached me at dawn. My mouth was opened, and I kept silent no longer.
Yahweh's word came to me:

"Son of man, those living in these ruins on Israel's soil are saying, 'Abraham was only one man, yet he took possession of the land. But we are numerous; to us the land is surely handed over to hold.'
So tell them: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: You eat meat with the blood in it, lift your eyes to your idols, and shed blood. Should you then possess the land?
You lean on your swords, you practice abominations, and every man of you defiles the wife of his neighbor. Should you then possess the land?'{c}

"Say this to them: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: As I live, those in the ruins will fall by the sword, those in the open country I will give to the wild animals to be devoured, and those in the strongholds and caves will die of plague.
I will turn the land into a waste and a horror, and the pride of its strength will cease. Israel's mountains will be so desolate that no one will pass through them.
Then they will know that I am Yahweh, when I turn the land into a waste and a horror for all the abominations they have done.'

"As for you, son of man, your people's children are talking about you by the walls and in the doorways of the houses. One says to another, every man to his brother, 'Let us go and hear what word comes from Yahweh.'

They come to you as people do, and sit before you as my people, and they hear your words, but they do not act on them. With their mouths they show much love,{d} but their hearts chase after their own gain.
To them you are like a love song, sung by one with a lovely voice who plays the instrument well. They hear your words, but they do not act on them.
Yet when this comes—and it is coming!—they will know that a prophet has been among them."

notes.text: Hebrew shofar, also in vv. 4–6.

Hebrew "in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month." On the spring-start calendar the tenth month is Tevet; the date falls in January 585 BC, about five months after the city fell. The Greek has "in the tenth year … in the twelfth month," and some ancient witnesses have "the eleventh year."
The Greek lacks most of vv. 25–26, from "You eat meat" to the end of v. 26.
Or "they act out lust"; the Hebrew is uncertain. The Greek has "falsehood is in their mouth."

verses.text: Yahweh's word came to me:

"Son of man, prophesy against Israel's shepherds. Prophesy, and say to them, to the shepherds: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Woe to Israel's shepherds, who have been tending only themselves! Is it not the flock that shepherds ought to tend?
You eat the fat,{a} you dress in the wool, you slaughter the fatlings, but the flock you do not tend.

The weak you have not made strong, the sick you have not healed, the injured you have not bandaged, the strays you have not brought back, the lost you have not sought; with force and harshness you have ruled them.
So they were scattered for lack of a shepherd, and once scattered they became food for every wild beast.
My sheep wandered over every mountain and every high hill; across the whole face of the earth my sheep were scattered, with no one searching or seeking for them.
"'So, you shepherds, hear Yahweh's word:

As I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, because my sheep have become plunder, because my sheep have become food for every wild beast for lack of a shepherd, since my shepherds did not search for my sheep but tended themselves and not my flock—
therefore, you shepherds, hear Yahweh's word.

The Lord Yahweh says this: Look, I am against the shepherds, and I will demand my flock from their hand. I will stop them from tending the flock, so that the shepherds will tend themselves no longer. I will snatch my sheep from their jaws, and they will no longer be food for them.
"'For the Lord Yahweh says this: Here I am; I myself will search for my sheep and look after them.

As a shepherd looks after his herd on the day he is among his scattered sheep, so I will look after my sheep. I will rescue them from every place where they were scattered on a day of cloud and thick darkness.

I will bring them out from the peoples, gather them from the lands, and bring them into their own soil. I will pasture them on Israel's mountains, by the ravines, and in every inhabited place in the land.
In good pasture I will feed them, and on the lofty mountains of Israel their grazing ground will be. There they will lie down in a good fold and feed on rich pasture on Israel's mountains.
I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I myself will give them rest, declares the Lord Yahweh.
The lost I will seek, the strayed I will bring back, the injured I will bind up, and the sick I will strengthen; but the fat and the strong I will destroy.{b} I will shepherd them with justice.
"'As for you, my flock, the Lord Yahweh says this: I am going to judge between one sheep and another, between rams and male goats.
Is it not enough for you to feed on the best pasture? Must you also tread down with your feet whatever pasture is left? Or to drink clear water, that you must muddy the rest with your feet?
Must my sheep eat the ground your hooves have trodden and drink the water your hooves have fouled?
"'So the Lord Yahweh says this to them: Here I am; I myself will judge between the fat sheep and the lean.
Because you shove with flank and shoulder and butt all the weak ones with your horns until you have scattered them abroad,
I will save my flock; no longer will they be plunder. I will judge between one sheep and another.
Over them I will set up one shepherd, my servant David, to pasture them. He will feed them himself and be a shepherd to them.
I, Yahweh, will be their God, and my servant David will be prince among them. I, Yahweh, have spoken.
"'With them I will cut a covenant of peace and banish the wild beasts from the land, so that in the wilderness they can dwell in safety and in the woods they can sleep.
I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing.{c} I will send down the rain in its season; there will be showers of blessing.

The trees of the field will yield their fruit and the land its produce, and they will be secure on their own soil. They will know that I am Yahweh when I break the bars of their yoke and rescue them from the hand of those who enslaved them.
No longer will they be plunder for the nations, nor will the land's wild beasts devour them. They will live in safety, with no one to frighten them.
I will raise up for them a planting renowned for its yield,{d} and no longer will they be swept away by famine in the land or bear the scorn of the nations.
Then they will know that I, Yahweh their God, am with them, and that they, Israel's house, are my people, declares the Lord Yahweh.
You are my sheep, the sheep of my pasture; you are human,{e} and I am your God, declares the Lord Yahweh.'"

notes.text: So the Hebrew vowels; with different vowels, and the Greek, "the milk."
So the Hebrew; the Greek has "the strong I will guard," reading a similar Hebrew word.
Or "I will make them a blessing around my hill." The Greek reads "I will settle them around my mountain."
Hebrew "a planting for a name"; the Greek has "a plant of peace."
Hebrew adam, "humankind," the word in the title "son of man" (ben adam; see the note at 2:1). The Greek lacks "you are human."

verses.text: Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir{a} and prophesy against it.
Say to it: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: I am coming against you, Mount Seir; I will stretch out my hand against you and make you a desolate waste.
Your towns I will turn into ruins, and you yourself will become a desolation. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
"'Because you nursed an age-old hatred and handed Israel's people over to the power of the sword at the time of their disaster, the time of their final punishment,
therefore, as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I will deliver you up to bloodshed, and bloodshed will hound you. Since you did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will hound you.{b}
Mount Seir I will turn into a waste and a horror, and from it I will cut off all who pass to and fro.
I will fill its mountains with its slain; on your hills and in your valleys and in all your ravines those slain by the sword will fall.
A desolation forever I will make you, and your towns will not be inhabited.{c} Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
"'Because you said, "These two nations and these two lands will be mine, and we will take possession of them"—though Yahweh was there—

therefore, as I live, declares the Lord Yahweh, I will deal with you in keeping with the anger and jealousy you showed out of your hatred for them. I will make myself known among them{d} when I judge you.
Then you will know that I, Yahweh, have heard all the insults you uttered against Israel's mountains when you said, "They lie desolate; they have been handed to us to devour."
With your mouths you made yourselves great against me and piled up your words against me. I heard it.
"'The Lord Yahweh says this: While the whole earth rejoices, I will make you a desolation.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of Israel's house because it was made desolate, so I will deal with you. A desolation you will be, Mount Seir, you and all Edom, every bit of it. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.'"

notes.text: See the note at 25:8.
The Hebrew of this verse is difficult; "blood" may also hint at Edom's name (compare Hebrew dam, "blood," and adom, "red").
So the Hebrew margin; the Hebrew text may be read "will not return."
The Greek has "to you."

verses.text: "And you, son of man, prophesy to Israel's mountains and say: 'Mountains of Israel, hear Yahweh's word.
The Lord Yahweh says this: Your enemy jeered over you, "Aha! Those age-old heights{a} are ours to hold now!"

So prophesy and say: The Lord Yahweh says this: Because they made you desolate and hounded you from every side, until the remaining nations owned you, and you have become the talk of gossiping tongues and the slander of the people,

therefore, mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord Yahweh. The Lord Yahweh says this to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys, to the desolate ruins and the deserted towns that have become plunder and a mockery to the rest of the nations around:

the Lord Yahweh says this: In the fire of my jealousy I have spoken against the rest of the nations and against all Edom, who with wholehearted glee and contempt claimed my land as their own possession, so as to drive out its pasture and plunder it.{b}

So prophesy concerning Israel's soil and tell the mountains and the hills, the ravines and the valleys: The Lord Yahweh says this: In my jealousy and my fury I speak, because you have endured the nations' scorn.
So the Lord Yahweh says this: I lift my hand and swear that the nations around you will themselves endure scorn.
"'But you, mountains of Israel, will put out your branches and bear your fruit for my people Israel, for they will soon come home.
For see, I am for you; I will turn my face to you, and plowmen and sowers will work you.
I will multiply people upon you, the whole house of Israel, all of it. The towns will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt.

I will multiply on you both human and beast; they will increase and be fruitful. I will settle you as you were in former times and treat you better than at your beginning. Then you will know that I am Yahweh.
I will make people walk upon you, my people Israel. They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance; never again will you rob them of their children.
"'The Lord Yahweh says this: Because people say to you, "You devour human beings and rob your nation of its children,"
therefore you will devour people no more or rob your nation{c} of its children, declares the Lord Yahweh.
I will no longer let you hear the nations' taunts; you will bear the peoples' scorn no more, and you will no longer make your nation stumble,{d} declares the Lord Yahweh.'"
Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, when Israel's house lived on their own soil, they defiled it by their conduct and their deeds. In my sight their conduct was like the impurity of a woman in her monthly period.
So I emptied out my wrath upon them, because of the blood spilled on the land and the idols that had polluted it.
I scattered them among the nations, and they were dispersed through the lands. By their conduct and their deeds I judged them.
But wherever they came among the nations, they profaned my holy name, for people said of them, 'These are Yahweh's people, yet they had to leave his land.'
I cared, though, for my holy name, which Israel's house profaned among the nations where they went.
"So say to Israel's house: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: Not for your sake am I about to act, house of Israel, but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations where you went.

I will show the holiness of my great name, which has been profaned among the nations, the name you profaned in their midst. And the nations will know that I am Yahweh, declares the Lord Yahweh, when through you I show myself holy before their eyes.{e}
"'I will take you from the nations, gather you from all the lands, and bring you to your own soil.
I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean from all your impurities; from all your idols I will cleanse you.
I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you. I will take the heart of stone out of your body and give you a heart of flesh.
I will put my Spirit{f} within you and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you will keep my rulings and carry them out.
In the land I granted to your fathers you will dwell; you will be a people to me, and I will be God to you.
I will save you from all your impurities. I will call to the grain and make it abound, and I will lay no famine on you.
I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the produce of the field, so that among the nations you will never again bear the shame of hunger.
Then you will remember your evil ways and your deeds that were not good, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and your abominations.
Not for your sake am I doing this, declares the Lord Yahweh—be sure of that. Be ashamed and humiliated for your ways, house of Israel.
"'The Lord Yahweh says this: On the day I cleanse you from all your iniquities, I will resettle the towns, and the ruins will be rebuilt.
The desolate land will be worked, where once it lay a waste before the eyes of every passerby.
They will say, "This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden, and the towns that were ruined, desolate, and torn down are now fortified and inhabited."
Then the nations left around you will know that I, Yahweh, have rebuilt what was torn down and replanted what was desolate. I, Yahweh, have spoken, and I will do it.
"'The Lord Yahweh says this: Once more I will let Israel's house seek this from me, and I will do it for them: I will make their people as many as a flock.
Like the flock for sacrifices, like Jerusalem's flock at her appointed feasts, so will the ruined towns be filled with flocks of people. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.'"

notes.text: Or "the everlasting high places."
The Hebrew of the last clause is difficult.
So the Hebrew margin and the Greek; the Hebrew text has "make your nation stumble."
The Greek lacks this clause.

Papyrus 967, one of the earliest known Greek manuscripts of Ezekiel (about AD 200), is reported to lack the passage from here ("And the nations will know…") through 36:38, and to place chapter 37 after chapters 38–39. Some scholars see this as evidence of an earlier edition of the book; others think the passage was lost by accident. These details are given as reported in scholarly literature.
Or "my spirit"; Hebrew ruach, also "wind" or "breath" (see 37:1–14).

verses.text: Yahweh's hand came on me, and he carried me out by Yahweh's Spirit{a} and set me down in the middle of the valley,{b} and it was full of bones.
He led me all around among them, and I saw a great many of them lying on the valley floor, and they were bone-dry.
He asked me, "Son of man, can these bones come to life?" I answered, "Lord Yahweh, only you know."
Then he said to me, "Prophesy over these bones and tell them: Dry bones, hear Yahweh's word!
The Lord Yahweh says this to these bones: I am going to bring breath{c} into you, and you will live.
I will lay sinews on you, make flesh grow over you, cover you with skin, and put breath in you, and you will live. Then you will know that I am Yahweh."
So I prophesied as I had been commanded. While I prophesied a sound broke out, a clattering, and the bones drew together, bone joining bone.
As I watched, sinews were on them, flesh had grown, and skin covered them over, but there was no breath in them.

Then he said to me, "Prophesy to the breath; prophesy, son of man, and say to the breath: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: From the four winds come, breath, and blow into these slain, so that they may live.'"
So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath entered them; they came to life and rose to their feet, an exceedingly vast army.
Then he said to me, "Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel. They keep saying, 'Our bones are dried up, our hope has perished; we are cut off, every one of us.'
So prophesy and say to them: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: My people, I am going to open your graves and raise you up out of them, and I will bring you to Israel's soil.
You will know that I am Yahweh, my people, when I open your graves and raise you up out of them.
I will put my Spirit within you, and you will live, and I will settle you on your own soil. Then you will know that I, Yahweh, have spoken and have done it, declares Yahweh.'"
Yahweh's word came to me:

"You, son of man, take a stick{d} and write on it, 'For Judah and for the Israelites joined with him.' Then take another stick and write on it, 'For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all Israel's house joined with him.'
Bring them together into one stick for yourself, so that they become one in your hand.
When your people's children ask you, 'Will you not explain to us what you mean by these?'

tell them, 'The Lord Yahweh says this: I am going to take the stick of Joseph, which is in Ephraim's hand, and the tribes of Israel joined with him, and I will put them with it, with Judah's stick, and make them a single stick, and they will be one in my hand.'{e}
The sticks on which you write are to be in your hand before their eyes.
Then tell them: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: I am going to take the Israelites from among the nations where they have gone. I will gather them from every side and bring them to their own soil.
I will make them one nation in the land, on Israel's mountains, and one king will be king over all of them. They will no longer be two nations, never again divided into two kingdoms.

They will no longer defile themselves with their idols, their detestable things, or any of their rebellions. I will save them from all the backslidings by which they sinned{f} and will cleanse them. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
"'My servant David will be king over them, and there will be one shepherd for them all. They will walk in my rulings and keep my statutes and do them.

They will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, where your fathers lived. There they will dwell forever, they and their sons and their sons' sons, with David my servant as their prince for all time.
I will make a covenant of peace with them; an everlasting covenant it will be. I will establish them and multiply them,{g} and I will set my sanctuary among them forever.
My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be my people.
Then the nations will know that I, Yahweh, make Israel holy, when my sanctuary is among them forever.'"

notes.text: Or "by the spirit of Yahweh"; Hebrew ruach, which can mean "spirit," "breath," or "wind." The word plays through vv. 1–14.
Or "plain"; the same word as in 3:22–23.
Hebrew ruach, also in vv. 6, 8–10; in v. 9 it is also "the four winds."
Or "a piece of wood," perhaps a wooden writing tablet; also in vv. 16–20.
So the Hebrew; the Greek has "one stick in the hand of Judah."
Probable reading, following the Greek; the Hebrew has "from all their dwelling places in which they sinned."
The Greek lacks "I will establish them and multiply them."

verses.text: Yahweh's word came to me:
"Son of man, turn your face toward Gog,{a} of the land of Magog,{b} the chief prince{c} of Meshech and Tubal, and prophesy against him.
Say: 'The Lord Yahweh says this: I am coming against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal.

I will turn you around, put hooks in your jaws, and lead you out with your whole army, horses and horsemen, all of them splendidly equipped, a vast company with large and small shields, every one of them wielding swords.
